For cases where the member is not normal to the plating, the section properties must be calculated in accordance with the appropriate classification society rules for the ship in question.

TRF-035.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-035.text: L shall be taken as the ship's rule length used by the classification society.
TRF-035.normalized: L shall be taken as the ship's rule length used by the classification society.

TRF-036.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-036.text: An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1. Table 4-1 values (ice class: hi, h in metres): IA Super: 1.0, 0.35; IA: 0.8, 0.30; IB: 0.6, 0.25; IC: 0.4, 0.22.
TRF-036.normalized: An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1. Table 4-1 values (ice class: hi, h in metres): IA Super: 1.0, 0.35; IA: 0.8, 0.30; IB: 0.6, 0.25; IC: 0.4, 0.22.

TRF-037.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-037.text: The design ice pressure is determined by the formula p = c_d*c_p*c_a*p_0 [MPa] (4.1), where c_d is a factor which takes account of the influence of the size and engine output of the ship. The maximum value is c_d = 1. It is calculated using c_d = (a*k + b)/1000 (4.2).
TRF-037.normalized: The design ice pressure is determined by the formula p = c_d*c_p*c_a*p_0 [MPa] (4.1), where c_d is a factor which takes account of the influence of the size and engine output of the ship. The maximum value is c_d = 1. It is calculated using c_d = (a*k + b)/1000 (4.2).

TRF-039.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-039.text: Delta is the displacement of the ship at a maximum ice class draught [t] (see section 2.2). P is the actual continuous engine output of the ship [kW] (see section 3.1) available when sailing in ice. If additional power sources are available for propulsion power (e.g. shaft motors) in addition to the power of the main engine(s), they shall also be included in the total engine output used as the basis for hull scantling calculations. The engine output used for the calculation of the hull scantlings shall be clearly stated on the shell expansion drawing. cp is a factor that reflects the magnitude of the load expected in the hull area in question relative to the bow area. The value of cp is given in Table 4-3. ca is a factor which takes account of the probability that the full length of the area under consideration will be under pressure at the same time. It is calculated using the formula: l (4.4) ca = l0 , maximum 1.0, minimum 0.35, l0 = 0.6 m. a Values of la are given in Table 4-4. po is the nominal ice pressure; the value 5.6 MPa shall be used.
TRF-039.normalized: Use displacement_Delta_t at maximum ice-class draught. total_propulsion_power_for_scantlings_kW shall include the main engine and every additional propulsion power source and shall be stated on the shell expansion drawing. Select c_p from Table 4-3. Compute c_a = clamp(l_a/l_0, 0.35, 1.0), where l_0 = 0.6 m. Use nominal_ice_pressure_p_0_MPa = 5.6.

TRF-040.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-040.text: In addition, the following areas shall be strengthened: Fore foot: For ice class IA Super, the shell plating below the ice belt from the stem to a position five main frame spacings abaft of the point where the bow profile departs from the keel line shall be ice-strengthened in the same way as the bow region. Upper bow ice belt: For ice classes IA Super and IA on ships with an open water service speed equal to or exceeding 18 knots, the shell plate from the upper limit of the ice belt to 2 m above it and from the stem to a position at least 0.2 L abaft of the forward perpendicular shall be ice-strengthened in the same way as the midbody region. A similar strengthening of the bow region is also advisable for a ship with a lower service speed when, on the basis of the model tests, for example, it is evident that the ship will have a high bow wave. Sidescuttles shall not be situated in the ice belt. If the weather deck on any part of the ship is situated below the upper limit of the ice belt (e.g. in the way of the well of a raised quarter decker), the bulwark shall be provided with at least the same strength as is required for the shell in the ice belt. The strength of the construction of the freeing ports shall meet the same requirements.
TRF-040.normalized: IF iceClass = 'IA Super', THEN forefoot_shell_strengthening_status = bow_region_equivalent for the specified five-main-frame-spacing extent. IF iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA'} AND open_water_service_speed_kn >= 18, THEN upper_bow_ice_belt_strengthening_status = midbody_equivalent for the area from the ice-belt upper limit to 2 m above it and at least 0.2*L aft of the forward perpendicular. sidescuttle_in_ice_belt = false. IF weather_deck_below_ice_belt_upper_limit = true, THEN bulwark_strength_status and freeing_port_strength_status shall meet the ice-belt shell requirement. The lower-speed model-test sentence is advisory and is not encoded as a mandatory constraint.

TRF-041.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-041.text: For transverse framing, the thickness of the shell plating shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(f_1*p_pl/sigma_y) + t_c [mm] (4.5). For longitudinal framing, the thickness shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(p/(f_2*sigma_y)) + t_c [mm] (4.6).
TRF-041.normalized: For transverse framing, the thickness of the shell plating shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(f_1*p_pl/sigma_y) + t_c [mm] (4.5). For longitudinal framing, the thickness shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(p/(f_2*sigma_y)) + t_c [mm] (4.6).

TRF-042.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-042.text: f_2 = 0.4/(h/s) + 0.6 where h/s <= 1; f_2 = 1.4 - 0.4*(h/s) where 1 <= h/s <= 1.8. Here h is as given in section 4.2.1 and sigma_y is the yield stress of the material [N/mm^2]. Use sigma_y = 235 N/mm^2 for normal-strength hull structural steel and sigma_y = 315 N/mm^2 or higher for high-strength hull structural steel. If steels with different yield stress are used, actual accepted values may be substituted. The abrasion and corrosion increment t_c shall normally be 2 mm; a lower approved value may be used for a suitable maintained special surface coating.
TRF-042.normalized: f_2 = 0.4/(h/s) + 0.6 where h/s <= 1; f_2 = 1.4 - 0.4*(h/s) where 1 <= h/s <= 1.8. Here h is as given in section 4.2.1 and sigma_y is the yield stress of the material [N/mm^2]. Use sigma_y = 235 N/mm^2 for normal-strength hull structural steel and sigma_y = 315 N/mm^2 or higher for high-strength hull structural steel. If steels with different yield stress are used, actual accepted values may be substituted. The abrasion and corrosion increment t_c shall normally be 2 mm; a lower approved value may be used for a suitable maintained special surface coating.

TRF-043.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-043.text: The vertical extension of the ice strengthening of framing shall be at least as given in Table 4- 6. Where an upper bow ice belt is required (see 4.3.1), the ice-strengthened part of the framing shall be extended to at least the top of this ice belt. Where the ice-strengthening would go beyond a deck, the top or bottom plating of a tank or tank top by no more than 250 mm, it can be terminated at that deck, top or bottom plating of the tank or tank top. Table 4-6 values: IA Super framing above UIWL 1.2 m; below LIWL bow down to tank top or below top of floors, midbody 2.0 m, stern 1.6 m. IA, IB and IC framing above UIWL 1.0 m; below LIWL bow 1.6 m, midbody 1.3 m, stern 1.0 m.
TRF-043.normalized: Set the vertical extent of framing ice strengthening from Table 4-6. IF upper_bow_ice_belt_required = true, THEN framing_ice_strengthening_upper_extent >= upper_bow_ice_belt_top. IF extension_beyond_adjacent_deck_or_tank_boundary_mm <= 250, THEN termination_at_that_boundary is permitted. Table 4-6 values: IA Super framing above UIWL 1.2 m; below LIWL bow down to tank top or below top of floors, midbody 2.0 m, stern 1.6 m. IA, IB and IC framing above UIWL 1.0 m; below LIWL bow 1.6 m, midbody 1.3 m, stern 1.0 m.

TRF-044.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-044.text: The section modulus of a main or intermediate transverse frame shall be calculated using Z = p*s*h*l/(m_t*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.7), and the effective shear area shall be calculated using A = sqrt(3)*f_3*p*h*s/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.8), where p is the ice pressure from 4.2.2, s is the frame spacing, h is the load-area height from 4.2.1, l is the frame span, m_t = 7*m_0/(7 - 5*h/l), f_3 = 1.2, sigma_y is the yield stress from 4.3.2, and m_0 is selected from Table 4-7 for the applicable boundary condition. Table 4-7 m0 values: bulk carrier frames with top wing tanks 7; frames from tank top to main deck of a single-decked vessel 6; continuous frames between several decks or stringers 5.7; frames between two decks only 5.
TRF-044.normalized: Compute m_t = 7*m_0/(7 - 5*h/l), Z_cm3 = p_MPa*s_m*h_m*l_m/(m_t*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6, and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*1.2*p_MPa*h_m*s_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4. Select m_0 from Table 4-7 for the frame boundary condition. Table 4-7 m0 values: bulk carrier frames with top wing tanks 7; frames from tank top to main deck of a single-decked vessel 6; continuous frames between several decks or stringers 5.7; frames between two decks only 5.

TRF-045.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-045.text: Where less than 15% of the span, l, of the frame is situated within the ice-strengthening zone for frames as defined in 4.4.1, ordinary frame scantlings may be used.
TRF-045.normalized: Where less than 15% of the span, l, of the frame is situated within the ice-strengthening zone for frames as defined in 4.4.1, ordinary frame scantlings may be used.

TRF-046.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-046.text: The upper end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where a frame terminates above a deck or a stringer which is situated at or above the upper limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the part above the deck or stringer may have the scantlings required by the classification society for an non ice-strengthened ship and the upper end of an intermediate frame may be connected to the adjacent frames by a horizontal member with the same scantlings as the main frame.
TRF-046.normalized: The upper end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where a frame terminates above a deck or a stringer which is situated at or above the upper limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the part above the deck or stringer may have the scantlings required by the classification society for an non ice-strengthened ship and the upper end of an intermediate frame may be connected to the adjacent frames by a horizontal member with the same scantlings as the main frame.

TRF-047.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-047.text: The lower end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where an intermediate frame terminates below a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or ice stringer which is situated at or below the lower limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the lower end may be connected to the adjacent main frames by a horizontal member of the same scantlings as the main frames. Note that the main frames below the lower edge of the ice belt must be ice strengthened, see 4.4.1.
TRF-047.normalized: The lower end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where an intermediate frame terminates below a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or ice stringer which is situated at or below the lower limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the lower end may be connected to the adjacent main frames by a horizontal member of the same scantlings as the main frames. Note that the main frames below the lower edge of the ice belt must be ice strengthened, see 4.4.1.

TRF-048.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-048.text: The section modulus of a longitudinal frame shall be calculated using Z = f_4*p*h*l^2/(4*m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.9). The effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_4*f_5*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.10). The bracket shear area shall not be included in the actual frame shear area. Use f_4 = 1 - 0.2*h/s, f_5 = 2.16, p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, s as frame spacing, l as total frame span, m = 13.3 for a continuous beam with brackets unless a smaller factor is required by significantly different boundary conditions, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.
TRF-048.normalized: Compute f_4 = 1 - 0.2*h/s, Z_cm3 = f_4*p_MPa*h_m*l_m^2/(4*m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6, and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*f_4*2.16*p_MPa*h_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4. Use m = 13.3 for a continuous beam with brackets unless the actual end field requires a smaller factor. Exclude bracket area from actual_frame_shear_area.

TRF-049.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-049.text: Within the ice-strengthened area, all frames shall be effectively attached to all of the supporting structures. A longitudinal frame shall be attached by brackets to all supporting web frames and bulkheads. When a transversal frame terminates at a stringer or deck, a bracket or similar construction must be fitted. When a frame is running through the supporting structure, both sides of the web plate of the frame must be connected to the structure (by direct welding, collar plate or lug). When a bracket is installed, it must have at least the same thickness as the web plate of the frame and the edge must be appropriately stiffened against buckling.
TRF-049.normalized: Within the ice-strengthened area, all frames shall be effectively attached to all of the supporting structures. A longitudinal frame shall be attached by brackets to all supporting web frames and bulkheads. When a transversal frame terminates at a stringer or deck, a bracket or similar construction must be fitted. When a frame is running through the supporting structure, both sides of the web plate of the frame must be connected to the structure (by direct welding, collar plate or lug). When a bracket is installed, it must have at least the same thickness as the web plate of the frame and the edge must be appropriately stiffened against buckling.

TRF-050.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-050.text: The frames shall be attached to the shell by a double continuous weld. No scalloping is allowed (except when crossing shell plate butts).
TRF-050.normalized: The frames shall be attached to the shell by a double continuous weld. No scalloping is allowed (except when crossing shell plate butts).

TRF-051.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-051.text: The web thickness of the frames shall be at least the maximum of: h_w*sqrt(sigma_y)/C, where C = 805 for profiles and C = 282 for flat bars; half of the net shell-plating thickness t - t_c; and 9 mm. Where a deck, tank top, tank bottom or bulkhead is used in lieu of a frame, its plate thickness shall be calculated in the same way using the adjacent frame height h_w and C = 805.
TRF-051.normalized: The web thickness of the frames shall be at least the maximum of: h_w*sqrt(sigma_y)/C, where C = 805 for profiles and C = 282 for flat bars; half of the net shell-plating thickness t - t_c; and 9 mm. Where a deck, tank top, tank bottom or bulkhead is used in lieu of a frame, its plate thickness shall be calculated in the same way using the adjacent frame height h_w and C = 805.

TRF-052.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-052.text: Asymmetrical frames and frames which are not at right angles to the shell (web less than 90 degrees to the shell) shall be supported against tripping by brackets, intercoastals, stringers or similar, at a distance not exceeding 1,300 mm. For frames with spans greater than 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions and for all ice classes. For frames with spans less than or equal to 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions for ice class IA Super, to the bow and midbody regions for ice class IA, and to the bow region for ice classes IB and IC. Direct calculation methods may be applied to demonstrate the equivalent level of support provided by alternative arrangements.
TRF-052.normalized: IF frame_asymmetrical = true OR frame_web_angle_to_shell_deg < 90, THEN antitripping_support_spacing_mm <= 1300. IF frame_span_m > 4, THEN antitripping_support_scope = 'all regions/all ice classes'. IF frame_span_m <= 4, THEN required scope is all regions for IA Super, bow and midbody for IA, and bow for IB or IC. An alternative arrangement is acceptable only when equivalent_support_status_by_direct_calculation = demonstrated.

TRF-053.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-053.text: The section modulus of a stringer situated within the ice belt shall be calculated using Z = f_6*f_7*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.11), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_6*f_7*f_8*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.12). Use p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, p*h = 0.15 MN/m when the calculated product is less than 0.15 MN/m, l as stringer span, m from 4.4.3, f_6 = 0.9, f_7 = 1.8, f_8 = 1.2, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.
TRF-053.normalized: Set design_line_load_MN_m = max(p_MPa*h_m, 0.15). Compute Z_cm3 = 0.9*1.8*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m^2/(m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6 and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*0.9*1.8*1.2*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4, with m selected under 4.4.3.

TRF-054.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-054.text: The section modulus of a stringer situated outside the ice belt but supporting ice-strengthened frames shall be calculated using Z = f_9*f_10*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*(1 - h_s/l_s)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.13), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_9*f_10*f_11*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*(1 - h_s/l_s)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.14). Use p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, p*h = 0.15 MN/m when the calculated product is less than 0.15 MN/m, l as stringer span, m from 4.4.3, l_s as the distance to the adjacent ice stringer, h_s as the distance to the ice belt, f_9 = 0.80, f_10 = 1.8, f_11 = 1.2, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.
TRF-054.normalized: Set design_line_load_MN_m = max(p_MPa*h_m, 0.15) and outside_ice_belt_factor = 1 - h_s_m/l_s_m. Compute Z_cm3 = 0.80*1.8*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m^2/(m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*outside_ice_belt_factor*10^6 and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*0.80*1.8*1.2*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*outside_ice_belt_factor*10^4.

TRF-055.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-055.text: Narrow deck strips abreast of hatches and serving as ice stringers shall comply with the section modulus and shear area requirements given in 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 respectively. In the case of very long hatches, the classification society may permit the product p* h to be given a value of less than 0.15 but in no case less than 0.10.
TRF-055.normalized: Narrow deck strips abreast of hatches and serving as ice stringers shall comply with the section modulus and shear area requirements given in 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 respectively. In the case of very long hatches, the classification society may permit the product p* h to be given a value of less than 0.15 but in no case less than 0.10.

TRF-056.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-056.text: Regard shall be paid to the deflection of the ship's sides due to ice pressure with respect to very long (more than B/2) hatch openings, when designing weatherdeck hatch covers and their fittings.
TRF-056.normalized: Regard shall be paid to the deflection of the ship's sides due to ice pressure with respect to very long (more than B/2) hatch openings, when designing weatherdeck hatch covers and their fittings.

TRF-057.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-057.text: The ice load transferred to a web frame from an ice stringer or from longitudinal framing shall be F = f_12*p*h*S [MN] (4.15). When calculating c_a, use l_a = 2*S. If p*h is less than 0.15 MN/m, use 0.15 MN/m. Use f_12 = 1.8.
TRF-057.normalized: The ice load transferred to a web frame from an ice stringer or from longitudinal framing shall be F = f_12*p*h*S [MN] (4.15). When calculating c_a, use l_a = 2*S. If p*h is less than 0.15 MN/m, use 0.15 MN/m. Use f_12 = 1.8.

TRF-058.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-058.text: If the supported stringer is outside the ice belt, the force F shall be multiplied by (1- hs/ls), where hs and ls shall be as defined in section 4.5.2.
TRF-058.normalized: If the supported stringer is outside the ice belt, the force F shall be multiplied by (1- hs/ls), where hs and ls shall be as defined in section 4.5.2.

TRF-059.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-059.text: The effective shear area of a web frame shall be calculated using A = sqrt(3)*alpha*f_13*Q/sigma_y*10^4 [cm^2] (4.16), where Q is the maximum calculated shear force under the ice load F from 4.6.1, f_13 = 1.1, alpha is selected from Table 4-8, and sigma_y is the yield stress from 4.3.2. Table 4-8 (Af/Aw: alpha, gamma): 0:1.5,0; 0.2:1.23,0.44; 0.4:1.16,0.62; 0.6:1.11,0.71; 0.8:1.09,0.76; 1.0:1.07,0.80; 1.2:1.06,0.83; 1.4:1.05,0.85; 1.6:1.05,0.87; 1.8:1.04,0.88; 2.0:1.04,0.89.

TRF-060.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-060.text: The section modulus of a web frame shall be calculated using Z = (M/sigma_y)*sqrt(1/(1 - (gamma*A/A_a)^2))*10^6 [cm^3] (4.17), where M is the maximum calculated bending moment under ice load F and shall be M = 0.193*F*L, gamma is selected from Table 4-8, A is the required shear area, and A_a = A_f + A_w is the actual cross-sectional area of the web frame.
TRF-060.normalized: Compute M_MNm = 0.193*F_MN*L_m and A_a_cm2 = A_f_cm2 + A_w_cm2. Then compute Z_cm3 = (M_MNm/sigma_y_N_mm2)*sqrt(1/(1 - (gamma*A_required_cm2/A_a_cm2)^2))*10^6, with gamma selected from Table 4-8.

TRF-061.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-061.text: The plate thickness of a shaped plate stem and, in the case of a blunt bow, any part of the shell where alpha >= 30o and psi >= 75o (see section 3.2.1 for angle definitions), shall be calculated according to formula 4.5, assuming that: s is the spacing of elements supporting the plate [m] pPL = p [MPa] (see section 4.3.2) la is the spacing of vertical supporting elements [m]. The stem and the part of a blunt bow defined above shall be supported by floors or brackets spaced no more than 0.6 m apart and with a thickness of at least half the plate thickness. The reinforcement of the stem shall extend from the keel to a point 0.75 m above the UIWL or, if an upper bow ice belt is required (see section 4.3.1), to the upper limit of this. The introduction of new propulsion arrangements with azimuthing thrusters, which provide improved manoeuvrability, will result in increased ice loading of the Stern region and the stern area. This fact should be considered in the design of the aft/stern structure.
TRF-061.normalized: The stem and the part of a blunt bow defined above shall be supported by floors or brackets spaced no more than 0.6 m apart and with a thickness of at least half the plate thickness.

TRF-062.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-062.text: In order to avoid very high loads on propeller blade tips, the minimum distance between the propeller(s) and the hull (including stern frame) should be no less than h0 (see 4.2.1).
TRF-062.normalized: In order to avoid very high loads on propeller blade tips, the minimum distance between the propeller(s) and the hull (including stern frame) should be no less than h0 (see 4.2.1).

TRF-063.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-063.text: On twin and triple screw ships, the ice strengthening of the shell and framing shall be extended to the tank top 1.5 metres forward and aft of the side propellers.
TRF-063.normalized: On twin and triple screw ships, the ice strengthening of the shell and framing shall be extended to the tank top 1.5 metres forward and aft of the side propellers.

TRF-064.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-064.text: The shafting and stern tubes of side propellers shall normally be enclosed within plated bossings. If detached struts are used, due consideration shall be taken of their design, strength and attachments to the hull.
TRF-064.normalized: The shafting and stern tubes of side propellers shall normally be enclosed within plated bossings. If detached struts are used, due consideration shall be taken of their design, strength and attachments to the hull.

TRF-065.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-065.text: The scantlings of the rudder post, rudder stock, pintles, steering engine etc. as well as the capability of the steering engine shall be determined according to the rules of the classification society. The maximum service speed of the ship to be used in these calculations shall, however, not be given a value lower than that stated below: IA Super 20 knots IA 18 knots IB 16 knots IC 14 knots If the actual maximum service speed of the ship is higher, that speed shall be used. The local scantlings of rudders must be determined assuming that the whole rudder belongs to the ice belt. Furthermore, the rudder plating and frames are to be designed using the ice pressure p for the plating and frames in the midbody region.
TRF-065.normalized: The maximum service speed of the ship to be used in these calculations shall not be given a value lower than: IA Super 20 knots, IA 18 knots, IB 16 knots, IC 14 knots.

TRF-066.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-066.text: For ice classes IA and IA Super, the rudder (the rudder stock and the upper part of the rudder) shall be protected from direct contact with intact ice by an ice knife that extends below the LIWL, if practicable (or equivalent means). Special consideration shall be given to the design of the rudder and the ice knife for ships with flap-type rudders.
TRF-066.normalized: For ice classes IA and IA Super, the rudder (the rudder stock and the upper part of the rudder) shall be protected from direct contact with intact ice by an ice knife that extends below the LIWL, if practicable (or equivalent means).

TRF-067.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-067.text: For ice classes IA and IA Super, due regard shall be paid to the large loads that arise when the rudder is forced out of the midship position when sailing astern in ice or into ice ridges. Suitable arrangements such as rudder stoppers shall be installed to absorb such loads.
TRF-067.normalized: For ice classes IA and IA Super, due regard shall be paid to the large loads that arise when the rudder is forced out of the midship position when sailing astern in ice or into ice ridges. Suitable arrangements such as rudder stoppers shall be installed to absorb such loads.

TRF-068.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-068.text: Relief valves for the hydraulic pressure in rudder turning mechanism(s) shall be installed. The components of the steering gear (e.g. rudder stock, rudder coupling, rudder horn etc.) shall be dimensioned to withstand loads causing yield stresses within the required diameter of the rudder stock.
TRF-068.normalized: hydraulic_rudder_relief_valve_present = true. Steering-gear components shall have dimensioning_analysis_status = compliant for the applicable loads and required rudder-stock diameter without exceeding yield stress.

TRF-069.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-069.text: These regulations apply to propulsion machinery covering open- and ducted-type propellers with a controllable pitch or fixed pitch design for ice classes IA Super, IA, IB and IC. The given propeller loads are the expected ice loads for the entire ship's service life under normal operational conditions, including loads resulting from the changing rotational direction of FP propellers. However, these loads do not cover off-design operational conditions, for example when a stopped propeller is dragged through ice. However, the load models of the regulations do not include propeller/ice interaction loads when ice enters the propeller of a turned azimuthing thruster from the side (radially).
TRF-069.normalized: The propulsion-machinery rule applies when iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'} and propeller_type IN {'open','ducted'} and pitch_type IN {'controllable','fixed'}. The design-load scope shall cover normal service-life propeller/ice loads, including FP reversal loads, and shall record that stopped-propeller dragging and radial ice entry into a turned azimuthing thruster are outside the prescribed load-model scope.

TRF-070.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-070.text: The regulations also apply to azimuthing and fixed thrusters for main propulsion, taking consideration of loads resulting from propeller/ice interaction and loads on the thruster body/ice interaction. The given azimuthing thruster body loads are the expected ice loads for the ship's service life under normal operational conditions. The local strength of the thruster body shall be sufficient to withstand local ice pressure when the thruster body is designed for extreme loads.
TRF-070.normalized: The regulations also apply to azimuthing and fixed thrusters for main propulsion, taking consideration of loads resulting from propeller/ice interaction and loads on the thruster body/ice interaction. The given azimuthing thruster body loads are the expected ice loads for the ship's service life under normal operational conditions. The local strength of the thruster body shall be sufficient to withstand local ice pressure when the thruster body is designed for extreme loads.

TRF-072.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-072.text: The materials of components exposed to sea water, such as propeller blades, propeller hubs, and thruster body, shall have an elongation of no less than 15% in a test specimen, the gauge length of which is five times the diameter. A Charpy V impact test shall be carried out for materials other than bronze and austenitic steel. An average impact energy value of 20 J based on three tests must be obtained at minus 10 oC. For nodular cast iron, average impact energy of 10 J at minus 10 oC is required accordingly.
TRF-072.normalized: For every seawater-exposed propeller, hub, or thruster-body material: elongation_test_percent >= 15 using gauge_length = 5*specimen_diameter. Unless material_type is bronze or austenitic steel, Charpy_V_test_count = 3 and average_impact_energy_J >= 20 at test_temperature_degC = -10. For nodular cast iron, average_impact_energy_J >= 10 at -10 deg C.

TRF-073.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-073.text: Materials exposed to sea water temperature shall be made of steel or another ductile material. An average impact energy value of 20 J, based on three tests, must be obtained at minus 10 oC. This requirement applies to the propeller shaft, blade bolts, CP mechanisms, shaft bolts, strut-pod connecting bolts etc. It does not apply to surface-hardened components, such as bearings and gear teeth. The nodular cast iron of a ferrite structure type may be used for relevant parts other than bolts. The average impact energy for nodular cast iron shall be a minimum of 10 J at minus 10 oC.
TRF-073.normalized: Seawater-temperature-exposed components shall use steel or another ductile material. For the listed shafts, bolts, CP mechanisms, and connecting components, Charpy_V_test_count = 3 and average_impact_energy_J >= 20 at -10 deg C, except for surface-hardened bearings and gear teeth. For permitted ferritic nodular cast-iron parts other than bolts, average_impact_energy_J >= 10 at -10 deg C.

TRF-074.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-074.text: If the highest point of the propeller is not at a depth of at least hi below the water surface when the ship is in ballast condition, the propulsion system shall be designed according to ice class IA for ice classes IB and IC.
TRF-074.normalized: If the highest point of the propeller is not at a depth of at least hi below the water surface when the ship is in ballast condition, the propulsion system shall be designed according to ice class IA for ice classes IB and IC.

TRF-075.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-075.text: Fb is the maximum force experienced during the lifetime of a ship that bends a propeller blade backwards when the propeller mills an ice block while rotating ahead. Ff is the maximum force experienced during the lifetime of a ship that bends a propeller blade forwards when the propeller mills an ice block while rotating ahead. Fb and Ff originate from different propeller/ice interaction phenomena, and do not occur simultaneously. Hence, they are to be applied to one blade separately.
TRF-075.normalized: Fb is the maximum force experienced during the lifetime of a ship that bends a propeller blade backwards when the propeller mills an ice block while rotating ahead. Ff is the maximum force experienced during the lifetime of a ship that bends a propeller blade forwards when the propeller mills an ice block while rotating ahead. Fb and Ff originate from different propeller/ice interaction phenomena, and do not occur simultaneously. Hence, they are to be applied to one blade separately.

TRF-076.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-076.text: Load cases 1-4 must be covered, as given in Table 6-4 below, for CP and FP propellers. To obtain blade ice loads for a reversing propeller, load case 5 must also be covered for FP propellers.
TRF-076.normalized: Load cases 1-4 must be covered, as given in Table 6-4 below, for CP and FP propellers. To obtain blade ice loads for a reversing propeller, load case 5 must also be covered for FP propellers.

TRF-077.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-077.text: where k is the shape parameter of the spectrum, Nice is the number of load cycles in the spectrum, and Fice is the random variable for ice loads on the blade, 0 <= Fice <= (Fice)max. The shape parameter k=0.75 shall be used for the ice force distribution of an open propeller and the shape parameter k=1.0 for that of a ducted propeller blade.
TRF-077.normalized: where k is the shape parameter of the spectrum, Nice is the number of load cycles in the spectrum, and Fice is the random variable for ice loads on the blade, 0 <= Fice <= (Fice)max. The shape parameter k=0.75 shall be used for the ice force distribution of an open propeller and the shape parameter k=1.0 for that of a ducted propeller blade.

TRF-078.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-078.text: The number of load cycles per propeller blade in the load spectrum shall be N_ice = k_1*k_2*k_3*N_class*n_n (6.14), where N_class is given in Table 6-6 and the propeller location factor k_1 is given in Table 6-7.
TRF-078.normalized: The number of load cycles per propeller blade in the load spectrum shall be N_ice = k_1*k_2*k_3*N_class*n_n (6.14), where N_class is given in Table 6-6 and the propeller location factor k_1 is given in Table 6-7.

TRF-079.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-079.text: The submersion factor k_2 is determined as follows: k_2 = 0.8 - f when f < 0; k_2 = 0.8 - 0.4*f when 0 <= f <= 1; k_2 = 0.6 - 0.2*f when 1 < f <= 2.5; and k_2 = 0.1 when f > 2.5 (6.15). The immersion function is f = (h_0 - H_ice)/(D/2) - 1 (6.16).
TRF-079.normalized: The submersion factor k_2 is determined as follows: k_2 = 0.8 - f when f < 0; k_2 = 0.8 - 0.4*f when 0 <= f <= 1; k_2 = 0.6 - 0.2*f when 1 < f <= 2.5; and k_2 = 0.1 when f > 2.5 (6.15). The immersion function is f = (h_0 - H_ice)/(D/2) - 1 (6.16).

TRF-080.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-080.text: For components that are subject to loads resulting from propeller/ice interaction with all the propeller blades, the number of load cycles (Nice) must be multiplied by the number of propeller blades (Z).
TRF-080.normalized: For components that are subject to loads resulting from propeller/ice interaction with all the propeller blades, the number of load cycles (Nice) must be multiplied by the number of propeller blades (Z).

TRF-081.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-081.text: The maximum forward and backward ice thrusts are T_f = 1.1*F_f [kN] (6.17) and T_b = 1.1*F_b [kN] (6.18). The design thrust along the propeller shaft line must be calculated using the formulae below. The greater value of the forward and backward direction loads shall be taken as the design load for both directions. Factors 2.2 and 1.5 take account of the dynamic magnification resulting from axial vibration. In a forward direction, T_r = T + 2.2*T_f [kN] (6.19). In a backward direction, T_r = 1.5*T_b [kN] (6.20).
TRF-081.normalized: Compute T_f_kN = 1.1*F_f_kN and T_b_kN = 1.1*F_b_kN. Compute forward_design_thrust_T_r_kN = hydrodynamic_bollard_thrust_T_kN + 2.2*T_f_kN and backward_design_thrust_T_r_kN = 1.5*T_b_kN. Set design_thrust_T_r_kN = max(forward_design_thrust_T_r_kN, backward_design_thrust_T_r_kN) for both directions.

TRF-082.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-082.text: If the hydrodynamic bollard thrust, T, is not known, it must be taken as given in Table 6-8.
TRF-082.normalized: If the hydrodynamic bollard thrust, T, is not known, it must be taken as given in Table 6-8.

TRF-083.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-083.text: n is the rotational propeller speed at MCR in bollard condition. If unknown, n must be attributed a value in accordance with Table 6-9.
TRF-083.normalized: n is the rotational propeller speed at MCR in bollard condition. If unknown, n must be attributed a value in accordance with Table 6-9.

TRF-084.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-084.text: For CP propellers, the propeller pitch, P0.7 shall correspond to MCR in bollard condition. If not known, P0.7 shall have a value equal to 0.7*P0.7n, where P0.7n is the propeller pitch at MCR in free running condition.
TRF-084.normalized: For CP propellers, the propeller pitch, P0.7 shall correspond to MCR in bollard condition. If not known, P0.7 shall have a value equal to 0.7*P0.7n, where P0.7n is the propeller pitch at MCR in free running condition.

TRF-085.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-085.text: n is the rotational propeller speed at MCR in bollard condition. If not known, n shall have a value according to Table 6-9.
TRF-085.normalized: Set propeller_speed_MCR_bollard_rpm to the known rotational propeller speed at MCR in bollard condition; otherwise select propeller_speed_MCR_bollard_rpm from Table 6-9.

TRF-086.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-086.text: For CP propellers, the propeller pitch, P0.7 shall correspond to MCR in bollard condition. If not known, P0.7 shall have a value equal to 0.7*P0.7n, where P0.7n is the propeller pitch at MCR in free running condition.
TRF-086.normalized: For CP propellers, the propeller pitch, P0.7 shall correspond to MCR in bollard condition. If not known, P0.7 shall have a value equal to 0.7*P0.7n, where P0.7n is the propeller pitch at MCR in free running condition.

TRF-087.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-087.text: All the torques and the inertia moments shall be reduced to the rotation speed of the component being examined.
TRF-087.normalized: All the torques and the inertia moments shall be reduced to the rotation speed of the component being examined.

TRF-088.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-088.text: If the maximum torque, Qemax, is unknown, it shall be accorded the value given in Table 6-10.
TRF-088.normalized: If the maximum torque, Qemax, is unknown, it shall be accorded the value given in Table 6-10.

TRF-089.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-089.text: If there is first blade order torsional resonance in the operational speed range or in the range 20% above and 20% below the maximum operating speed (bollard condition), the design torque (Qpeak) of the shaft component shall be determined by means of torsional vibration
TRF-089.normalized: If there is first blade order torsional resonance in the operational speed range or in the range 20% above and 20% below the maximum operating speed (bollard condition), the design torque Q_peak of the shaft component shall be determined by means of torsional vibration analysis, using frequency domain calculation as one of the two alternative methods.

TRF-090.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-090.text: Time domain calculations shall be calculated for the MCR condition, MCR bollard conditions and for blade order resonant rotational speeds so that the resonant vibration responses can be obtained.
TRF-090.normalized: Time domain calculations shall be calculated for the MCR condition, MCR bollard conditions and for blade order resonant rotational speeds so that the resonant vibration responses can be obtained.

TRF-091.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-091.text: The load sequence given in this chapter, for a case where a propeller is milling an ice block, shall be used for the strength evaluation of the propulsion line. The given load sequence is not intended for propulsion system stalling analyses.
TRF-091.normalized: The load sequence given in this chapter, for a case where a propeller is milling an ice block, shall be used for the strength evaluation of the propulsion line. The given load sequence is not intended for propulsion system stalling analyses.

TRF-092.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-092.text: The following load cases are intended to reflect the operational loads on the propulsion system, when the propeller interacts with ice, and the respective reaction of the complete system. The ice impact and system response causes loads in the individual shaft line components. The ice torque Qmax may be taken as a constant value in the complete speed range. When considerations at specific shaft speeds are performed, a relevant Qmax may be calculated using the relevant speed according to section 6.5.3.
TRF-092.normalized: The following load cases are intended to reflect the operational loads on the propulsion system, when the propeller interacts with ice, and the respective reaction of the complete system. The ice impact and system response causes loads in the individual shaft line components. The ice torque Qmax may be taken as a constant value in the complete speed range. When considerations at specific shaft speeds are performed, a relevant Qmax may be calculated using the relevant speed according to section 6.5.3.

TRF-093.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-093.text: Diesel engine plants without an elastic coupling shall be calculated at the least favourable phase angle for ice versus engine excitation, when calculated in the time domain. The engine firing pulses shall be included in the calculations and their standard steady state harmonics can be used.
TRF-093.normalized: Diesel engine plants without an elastic coupling shall be calculated at the least favourable phase angle for ice versus engine excitation, when calculated in the time domain. The engine firing pulses shall be included in the calculations and their standard steady state harmonics can be used.

TRF-094.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-094.text: If there is a blade order resonance just above the MCR speed, calculations shall cover rotational speeds up to 105% of the MCR speed.
TRF-094.normalized: If there is a blade order resonance just above the MCR speed, calculations shall cover rotational speeds up to 105% of the MCR speed.

TRF-095.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-095.text: For transient shaft-line analysis in the time domain, the propeller ice torque excitation is a sequence of half-sine blade impacts whose frequency follows propeller rotational speed. The torque from one blade impact is Q(phi) = C_q*Q_max*sin(phi*(180/alpha_i)) for 0 <= phi <= alpha_i plus integer revolutions (6.29); otherwise Q(phi) = 0 (6.30). C_q and alpha_i are given in Table 6-11.
TRF-095.normalized: For transient shaft-line analysis in the time domain, the propeller ice torque excitation is a sequence of half-sine blade impacts whose frequency follows propeller rotational speed. The torque from one blade impact is Q(phi) = C_q*Q_max*sin(phi*(180/alpha_i)) for 0 <= phi <= alpha_i plus integer revolutions (6.29); otherwise Q(phi) = 0 (6.30). C_q and alpha_i are given in Table 6-11.

TRF-096.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-096.text: If a speed drop occurs until the main engine is at a standstill, this indicates that the engine may not be sufficiently powered for the intended service task. For the consideration of loads, the maximum occurring torque during the speed drop process must be used.
TRF-096.normalized: If a speed drop occurs until the main engine is at a standstill, this indicates that the engine may not be sufficiently powered for the intended service task. For the consideration of loads, the maximum occurring torque during the speed drop process must be used.

TRF-097.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-097.text: For a time-domain calculation, if the simulated response torque does not include both the engine mean torque and the propeller mean torque, obtain the response torque using Q_peak = Q_emax + Q_rtd (6.32), where Q_rtd is the maximum simulated torque from the time-domain analysis.
TRF-097.normalized: If the time-domain response does not already include the engine and propeller mean torques, compute Q_peak = Q_emax + Q_rtd.

TRF-098.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-098.text: For frequency-domain calculations, blade-order and twice-blade-order excitation may be used. The propeller ice torque is Q_F(phi) = Q_max*(C_q0 + C_q1*sin(Z*E_0*phi + alpha_1) + C_q2*sin(2*Z*E_0*phi + alpha_2)) [kNm] (6.33). The coefficients and excitation cases are given in Table 6-12.
TRF-098.normalized: For frequency-domain calculations, blade-order and twice-blade-order excitation may be used. The propeller ice torque is Q_F(phi) = Q_max*(C_q0 + C_q1*sin(Z*E_0*phi + alpha_1) + C_q2*sin(2*Z*E_0*phi + alpha_2)) [kNm] (6.33). The coefficients and excitation cases are given in Table 6-12.

TRF-099.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-099.text: The design torque for a frequency-domain excitation case must be obtained using Q_peak = Q_emax + Q_vib + (Q_max_n*C_q0)*(I_e/I_t) + Q_rf1 + Q_rf2 (6.34). Q_rf1 and Q_rf2 are the first- and second-order torsional responses. If Q_emax is unknown, use Table 6-10. Scale every torque to the shaft revolutions of the component in question.
TRF-099.normalized: For each frequency-domain excitation case, compute Q_peak = Q_emax + Q_vib + (Q_max_n*C_q0)*(I_e/I_t) + Q_rf1 + Q_rf2 and scale all torque values to the component shaft speed.

TRF-100.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-100.text: The aim of time domain torsional vibration simulations is to estimate the extreme torsional load for the ship's lifespan. The simulation model can be taken from the normal lumped mass elastic torsional vibration model, including damping. For a time domain analysis, the model should include the ice excitation at the propeller, other relevant excitations and the mean torques provided by the prime mover and hydrodynamic mean torque in the propeller. The calculations should cover variation of phase between the ice excitation and prime mover excitation. This is extremely relevant to propulsion lines with directly driven combustion engines. Time domain calculations shall be calculated for the MCR condition, MCR bollard conditions and for resonant speed, so that the resonant vibration responses can be obtained. For frequency domain calculations, the load should be estimated as a Fourier component analysis of the continuous sequence of half sine load sequences. First and second order blade components should be used for excitation.
TRF-100.normalized: For time-domain torsional analysis, the model shall include propeller ice excitation, other relevant excitations, prime-mover mean torque, hydrodynamic propeller mean torque, damping, and variation of phase between ice and prime-mover excitations. The analysis shall cover MCR, MCR bollard, and resonant speeds. For frequency-domain analysis, derive Fourier components from the continuous half-sine sequence and include first- and second-order blade excitation components.

TRF-101.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-101.text: The ultimate load resulting from blade failure by plastic bending around the blade root shall be calculated using F_ex = 300*c*t^2*sigma_ref1/(0.8*D - 2*r) [kN] (6.35), or by an appropriate stress analysis reflecting the non-linear plastic material behaviour of the actual blade. The load is assumed to act at radius 0.8R in the weakest blade direction. A blade is regarded as failed if the tip offset exceeds 10% of propeller diameter D. Use sigma_ref1 = 0.6*sigma_0.2 + 0.4*sigma_u [MPa], with c, t and r representing the actual chord length, maximum thickness, and cylindrical-root radius of the weakest section outside the root fillet.
TRF-101.normalized: Determine blade_failure_load_F_ex_kN by an approved non-linear stress analysis OR compute F_ex = 300*c*t^2*sigma_ref1/(0.8*D - 2*r), where sigma_ref1 = 0.6*sigma_0.2 + 0.4*sigma_u. Apply the load at 0.8R in the weakest direction. blade_failure_status = failed IF blade_tip_offset_m > 0.10*propeller_diameter_m.

TRF-102.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-102.text: The maximum spindle torque due to a blade-failure load acting at 0.8R shall be determined by appropriate stress analysis or Q_sex = max(C_LE0.8, 0.8*C_TE0.8)*C_spex*F_ex [kNm] (6.36), where C_spex = C_sp*C_fex = 0.7*(1 - ((4*EAR)/Z)^3) (6.37). If C_spex is below 0.3, a value of 0.3 shall be used. C_LE0.8 and C_TE0.8 are the leading-edge and trailing-edge portions of chord length at 0.8R.
TRF-102.normalized: Compute C_spex = max(0.3, 0.7*(1 - ((4*EAR)/Z)^3)) and Q_sex_kNm = max(C_LE0.8, 0.8*C_TE0.8)*C_spex*F_ex_kN, unless an appropriate stress analysis directly determines the maximum spindle torque.

TRF-103.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-103.text: Csp is a non-dimensional parameter taking account of the spindle arm Cfex is a non-dimensional parameter taking account of the reduction of the blade failure force at the location of the maximum spindle torque. If Cspex is below 0.3, a value of 0.3 shall to be used for Cspex. CLE0.8 is the leading edge portion of the chord length at 0.8R CTE0.8 is the trailing edge portion of the chord length at 0.8R.
TRF-103.normalized: Csp is a non-dimensional parameter taking account of the spindle arm Cfex is a non-dimensional parameter taking account of the reduction of the blade failure force at the location of the maximum spindle torque. If Cspex is below 0.3, a value of 0.3 shall to be used for Cspex. CLE0.8 is the leading edge portion of the chord length at 0.8R CTE0.8 is the trailing edge portion of the chord length at 0.8R.

TRF-104.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-104.text: The strength of the propulsion line shall be designed according to the pyramid strength principle. This means that the loss of the propeller blade shall not cause any significant damage to other propeller shaft line components.
TRF-104.normalized: The strength of the propulsion line shall be designed according to the pyramid strength principle. This means that the loss of the propeller blade shall not cause any significant damage to other propeller shaft line components.

TRF-105.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-105.text: Blade stresses shall be calculated for the design loads in section 6.5.1. Finite element analysis shall be used for final approval of all propellers. The simplified root-area estimate is sigma_st = C_1*M_BL/(100*c*t^2) [MPa] (6.38).
TRF-105.normalized: Blade stresses shall be calculated for the design loads in section 6.5.1. Finite element analysis shall be used for final approval of all propellers. The simplified root-area estimate is sigma_st = C_1*M_BL/(100*c*t^2) [MPa] (6.38).

TRF-106.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-106.text: The calculated blade stresses must satisfy sigma_ref2/sigma_st >= 1.3 (6.39). If finite element analysis is used for estimating the stresses, von Mises stresses shall be used. sigma_ref2 is the reference strength, defined as the lower of 0.7*sigma_u and 0.6*sigma_0.2 + 0.4*sigma_u. The fatigue design of the propeller blade is based on an estimated load distribution for the service life of the ship and the S-N curve for the blade material. An equivalent stress that produces the same fatigue damage as the expected load distribution shall be calculated, and the acceptability criterion for fatigue should be fulfilled as given in section 6.6.2.4. The equivalent stress is normalised for 10^8 cycles.
TRF-106.normalized: Require sigma_ref2_MPa/sigma_st_MPa >= 1.3, where sigma_ref2_MPa = min(0.7*sigma_u_MPa, 0.6*sigma_0_2_MPa + 0.4*sigma_u_MPa). If finite_element_analysis_used = true, stress_measure = von_Mises. Fatigue verification shall use the service-life load distribution and the material S-N curve to calculate an equivalent stress producing the same fatigue damage, normalized to 10^8 cycles, and shall satisfy the section 6.6.2.4 acceptability criterion.

TRF-108.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-108.text: The type of the SN-curve shall be selected to correspond with the material properties of the blade. If the SN-curve is unknown, the two slope SN curve shall be used.
TRF-108.normalized: The type of the SN-curve shall be selected to correspond with the material properties of the blade. If the SN-curve is unknown, the two slope SN curve shall be used.

TRF-109.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-109.text: The coefficients C1, C2, C3, and C4 are given in Table 6-14. The applicable range of Nice for calculating rho is 5x106 <= Nice <= 108.
TRF-109.normalized: The coefficients C1, C2, C3, and C4 are given in Table 6-14. The applicable range of Nice for calculating rho is 5x106 <= Nice <= 108.

TRF-110.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-110.text: At every blade location, the equivalent fatigue stress shall satisfy sigma_fl/sigma_fat >= 1.5 (6.45). Use sigma_fl = gamma_e1*gamma_e2*gamma_v*gamma_m*sigma_exp. If actual reduction factors are unavailable, use gamma_e1*gamma_e2 = 0.67, gamma_v = 0.75 and gamma_m = 0.75. Blade bolts, CP mechanism, propeller boss and propeller-shaft fitting shall have safety factors greater than 1.3 against yielding, greater than 1.5 against fatigue, and greater than 1.0 against yielding under blade-loss loads.
TRF-110.normalized: At every blade location, require sigma_fl/sigma_fat >= 1.5. If actual reduction factors are unavailable, use gamma_e1*gamma_e2 = 0.67, gamma_v = 0.75, and gamma_m = 0.75. For blade bolts, the CP mechanism, propeller boss, and propeller-shaft fitting, require safety_factor_yield > 1.3, safety_factor_fatigue > 1.5, and safety_factor_blade_loss_yield > 1.0.

TRF-111.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-111.text: The shafts and shafting components, such as the thrust and stern tube bearings, couplings, flanges and sealings, shall be designed to withstand the propeller/ice interaction loads as given in section 6.5. The safety factor must be at least 1.3 against yielding for extreme operational loads, 1.5 for fatigue loads and 1.0 against yielding for the blade failure load.
TRF-111.normalized: The shafts and shafting components, such as the thrust and stern tube bearings, couplings, flanges and sealings, shall be designed to withstand the propeller/ice interaction loads as given in section 6.5. The safety factor must be at least 1.3 against yielding for extreme operational loads, 1.5 for fatigue loads and 1.0 against yielding for the blade failure load.

TRF-112.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-112.text: The ultimate load resulting from total blade failure, as defined in section 6.5.4 should not cause yielding in shafts and shaft components. The loading shall consist of the combined axial, bending, and torsion loads, wherever this is significant. The minimum safety factor against yielding must be 1.0 for bending and torsional stresses.
TRF-112.normalized: The ultimate load resulting from total blade failure, as defined in section 6.5.4 should not cause yielding in shafts and shaft components. The loading shall consist of the combined axial, bending, and torsion loads, wherever this is significant. The minimum safety factor against yielding must be 1.0 for bending and torsional stresses.

TRF-113.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-113.text: The steering mechanism, the fitting of the unit, and the body of the thruster shall be designed to withstand the plastic bending of a blade without damage. The loss of a blade must be taken into account for the propeller blade orientation causing the maximum load on the component being studied. Top-down blade orientation typically places the maximum bending loads on the thruster body.
TRF-113.normalized: The steering mechanism, the fitting of the unit, and the body of the thruster shall be designed to withstand the plastic bending of a blade without damage. The loss of a blade must be taken into account for the propeller blade orientation causing the maximum load on the component being studied. Top-down blade orientation typically places the maximum bending loads on the thruster body.

TRF-114.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-114.text: The thruster must withstand the loads occurring when the design ice block defined in Table 6-3 impacts on the thruster body when the ship is sailing at a typical ice operating speed. Load cases for impact loads are given in Table 6-16. The contact geometry is estimated to be hemispherical in shape. If the actual contact geometry differs from the shape of the hemisphere, a sphere radius must be estimated so that the growth of the contact area as a function of penetration of ice corresponds as closely as possible to the actual geometrical shape penetration.
TRF-114.normalized: The thruster must withstand the loads occurring when the design ice block defined in Table 6-3 impacts on the thruster body when the ship is sailing at a typical ice operating speed. Load cases for impact loads are given in Table 6-16. The contact geometry is estimated to be hemispherical in shape. If the actual contact geometry differs from the shape of the hemisphere, a sphere radius must be estimated so that the growth of the contact area as a function of penetration of ice corresponds as closely as possible to the actual geometrical shape penetration.

TRF-116.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-116.text: For impacts on non-hemispherical areas, such as the impact on the nozzle, the equivalent impact sphere radius must be estimated using the equation below.
TRF-116.normalized: For impacts on non-hemispherical areas, such as the impact on the nozzle, the equivalent impact sphere radius must be estimated using the equation below.

TRF-118.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-118.text: The stresses on the thruster must be calculated for the extreme once-in-a-lifetime loads described in section 6.6.5. The nominal von Mises stresses on the thruster body must have a safety margin of 1.3 against the yielding strength of the material. At areas of local stress concentrations, stresses must have a safety margin of 1.0 against yielding. The slewing bearing, bolt connections and other components must be able to maintain operability without incurring damage that requires repair when subject to the loads given in sections 6.6.5.2 and 6.6.5.3 multiplied by a safety factor of 1.3.
TRF-118.normalized: The stresses on the thruster must be calculated for the extreme once-in-a-lifetime loads described in section 6.6.5. The nominal von Mises stresses on the thruster body must have a safety margin of 1.3 against the yielding strength of the material. At areas of local stress concentrations, stresses must have a safety margin of 1.0 against yielding. The slewing bearing, bolt connections and other components must be able to maintain operability without incurring damage that requires repair when subject to the loads given in sections 6.6.5.2 and 6.6.5.3 multiplied by a safety factor of 1.3.

TRF-119.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-119.text: Evaluating the global vibratory behavior of the thruster body is important, if the first blade order excitations are in the same frequency range with the thruster global modes of vibration, which occur when the propeller rotational speeds are in the high power range of the propulsion line. This evaluation is mandatory and it must be shown that there is either no global first blade order resonance at high operational propeller speeds (above 50% of maximum power) or that the structure is designed to withstand vibratory loads during resonance above 50% of maximum power.
TRF-119.normalized: Evaluating the global vibratory behavior of the thruster body is important, if the first blade order excitations are in the same frequency range with the thruster global modes of vibration, which occur when the propeller rotational speeds are in the high power range of the propulsion line. This evaluation is mandatory and it must be shown that there is either no global first blade order resonance at high operational propeller speeds (above 50% of maximum power) or that the structure is designed to withstand vibratory loads during resonance above 50% of maximum power.

TRF-120.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-120.text: When estimating thruster global natural frequencies in the longitudinal and transverse direction, the damping and added mass due to water must be taken into account. In addition to this, the effect of ship attachment stiffness must be modelled.
TRF-120.normalized: When estimating thruster global natural frequencies in the longitudinal and transverse direction, the damping and added mass due to water must be taken into account. In addition to this, the effect of ship attachment stiffness must be modelled.

TRF-121.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-121.text: As an alternative to sections 6.5 and 6.6, a comprehensive design study may be performed to the satisfaction of the Administration or the classification society in question. The study must be based on the ice conditions given for different ice classes in section 6.3. It must include both fatigue and maximum load design calculations and fulfil the pyramid strength principle, as given in section 6.6.1.
TRF-121.normalized: As an alternative to sections 6.5 and 6.6, a comprehensive design study may be performed to the satisfaction of the Administration or the classification society in question. The study must be based on the ice conditions given for different ice classes in section 6.3. It must include both fatigue and maximum load design calculations and fulfil the pyramid strength principle, as given in section 6.6.1.

TRF-123.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-123.text: The analysis must confirm that all components transmitting random (occasional) forces, excluding propeller blade, are not subjected to stress levels in excess of the yield stress of the component material, with a reasonable safety margin.
TRF-123.normalized: The analysis must confirm that all components transmitting random (occasional) forces, excluding propeller blade, are not subjected to stress levels in excess of the yield stress of the component material, with a reasonable safety margin.

TRF-125.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-125.text: A vibration analysis must be performed and demonstrate that the overall dynamic system is free of the harmful torsional resonances resulting from propeller/ice interaction.
TRF-125.normalized: A vibration analysis must be performed and demonstrate that the overall dynamic system is free of the harmful torsional resonances resulting from propeller/ice interaction.

TRF-126.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-126.text: The capacity of the air receivers must be sufficient to provide no less than 12 consecutive starts of the propulsion engine without reloading, if it has to be reversed for moving astern, or 6 consecutive starts if the propulsion engine does not have to be reversed for moving astern.
TRF-126.normalized: IF propulsion_engine_reversed_for_astern = true, THEN air_receiver_consecutive_start_capacity >= 12; otherwise air_receiver_consecutive_start_capacity >= 6.

TRF-127.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-127.text: If the air receivers serve any purposes other than starting the propulsion engine, they must have additional capacity sufficient for such purposes.
TRF-127.normalized: If the air receivers serve any purposes other than starting the propulsion engine, they must have additional capacity sufficient for such purposes.

TRF-128.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-128.text: The capacity of the air compressors must be sufficient for charging the air receivers from atmospheric to full pressure in one (1) hour, except for a ship with ice class IA Super, if its propulsion engine has to be reversed for going astern, in which case the compressor must be able to charge the receivers in half an hour.
TRF-128.normalized: The capacity of the air compressors must be sufficient for charging the air receivers from atmospheric to full pressure in one (1) hour, except for a ship with ice class IA Super, if its propulsion engine has to be reversed for going astern, in which case the compressor must be able to charge the receivers in half an hour.

TRF-129.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-129.text: The cooling water system shall be designed to secure the supply of cooling water when navigating in ice.
TRF-129.normalized: The cooling water system shall be designed to secure the supply of cooling water when navigating in ice.

TRF-130.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-130.text: For this purpose, at least one cooling water inlet chest shall be arranged as follows: 1. The sea inlet shall be situated near the centreline of the ship and well aft, if possible. 2. Guidance for designing the volume of the chest shall be around one cubic metre for every 750 kW in engine output of the ship, including the output of auxiliary engines necessary for the operation of the ship. 3. The chest shall be sufficiently high to allow ice to accumulate above the inlet pipe. 4. A pipe for discharge cooling water, allowing full capacity discharge, shall be connected to the chest. 5. The open area of the strainer plates shall be no less than four (4) times the inlet pipe sectional area. If there are difficulties in meeting the requirements of paragraphs 2 and 3 above, two smaller chests may be arranged for alternating the intake and discharge of cooling water. Otherwise, the arrangements and situation shall be as above. Heating coils may be installed in the upper part of the sea chest.
TRF-130.normalized: At least one cooling-water inlet chest shall satisfy: sea_inlet_location = near_centreline_and_well_aft_if_possible; recommended_chest_volume_m3 approximately total_relevant_engine_power_kW/750; ice_accumulation_space_above_inlet = true; full_capacity_discharge_pipe_connected = true; strainer_open_area_m2 >= 4*inlet_pipe_area_m2. If paragraphs 2 and 3 cannot be met, two smaller alternating intake/discharge chests may be used. Heating coils are optional.

TRF-131.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-131.text: Arrangements for using ballast water for cooling purposes may be useful as a reserve in terms of ballast, but cannot be accepted as a substitute for an inlet chest as described above.
TRF-131.normalized: Arrangements for using ballast water for cooling purposes may be useful as a reserve in terms of ballast, but cannot be accepted as a substitute for an inlet chest as described above.

TRF-132.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-132.text: The engine output shall be no less than P = f_1*f_2*f_3*(f_4*Delta + P_0) [kW], and in no case less than 740 kW for ice classes IB and IC.
TRF-132.normalized: The engine output shall be no less than P = f_1*f_2*f_3*(f_4*Delta + P_0) [kW], and in no case less than 740 kW for ice classes IB and IC.

TRF-133.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
TRF-133.text: 1. The upper edge of the warning triangle must be located vertically above the "ICE" mark, 1,000 mm higher than the Summer Load Line in fresh water but in no case higher than the deck line. The sides of the triangle must be 300 mm in length. 2. The ice class draught mark must be located 540 mm abaft of the centre of the load line ring or 540 mm abaft of the vertical line of the timber load line mark, if applicable. 3. The marks and figures must be cut out of 5 - 8 mm plate and then welded to the ship's side. The marks and figures must be painted in a red or yellow reflecting colour in order to make the marks and figures plainly visible, even in ice conditions. 4. The dimensions of all letters must be the same as those used in the load line mark.

The upper edge of the warning triangle must be located vertically above the "ICE" mark, 1,000 mm higher than the Summer Load Line in fresh water but in no case higher than the deck line. The sides of the triangle must be 300 mm in length. 2. The dimensions of all letters must be the same as those used in the load line mark.

I2-001.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-001.text: Rev.4 of this UR is to be uniformly implemented by the IACS Societies on ships contracted for construction on or after 1 Jan 2021.
I2-001.normalized: Apply UR I2 Rev.4 to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2021.

I2-002.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-002.text: This UR applies to Polar Class ships according to UR I1.
I2-002.normalized: This UR applies to Polar Class ships according to UR I1.

I2-003.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-003.text: The length LUI is the distance, in m, measured horizontally from the fore side of the stem at the intersection with the upper ice waterline (UIWL) to the after side of the rudder post, or the centre of the rudder stock if there is no rudder post. LUI is not to be less than 96%, and need not be greater than 97%, of the extreme length of the upper ice waterline (UIWL) measured horizontally from the fore side of the stem. In ships with unusual stern and bow arrangement the length LUI will be specially considered.
I2-003.normalized: The length LUI is the distance, in m, measured horizontally from the fore side of the stem at the intersection with the upper ice waterline (UIWL) to the after side of the rudder post, or the centre of the rudder stock if there is no rudder post. I2-004.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-004.text: The ship displacement DUI is the displacement, in kt, of the ship corresponding to the upper ice waterline (UIWL). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the displacement is to be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest displacement.

I2-005.text: The boundary between the bottom and lower regions is to be taken at the point where the shell is inclined 7 deg from horizontal.
I2-005.normalized: The boundary between the bottom and lower regions is to be taken at the point where the shell is inclined 7 deg from horizontal.

I2-006.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-006.text: If a ship is intended to operate astern in ice regions, the aft section of the ship is to be designed using the Bow and Bow Intermediate hull area requirements.
I2-006.normalized: If a ship is intended to operate astern in ice regions, the aft section of the ship is to be designed using the Bow and Bow Intermediate hull area requirements.

I2-008.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-008.text: (iii) Within the Bow area of all Polar Class ships, and within the Bow Intermediate Icebelt area of Polar Class PC6 and PC7, the ice load parameters are functions of the actual bow shape. I2-009.text: (iv) In other ice-strengthened areas, the ice load parameters (Pavg, bNonBow and wNonBow) are determined independently of the hull shape and based on a fixed load patch aspect ratio, AR = 3.6. I2-010.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-010.text: (vi) Design ice forces calculated according to I2.3.2.1 (iv) are applicable for ships which are assigned the Polar Class PC6 or PC7 and have a bow form with vertical sides. I2-011.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-011.text: (vii) For ships which are assigned the Polar Class PC6 or PC7, and equipped with bulbous bows, the design ice forces on the bow are to be determined according to I2.3.2.1 (iv). I2-013.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-013.text: (ix) Ship structures that are not directly subjected to ice loads may still experience inertial loads of stowed cargo and equipment resulting from ship/ice interaction. These inertial loads, based on accelerations determined by the Classification Society, are to be considered in the design of these structures. I2-014.text: (ii) The waterline length of the bow region is generally to be divided into 4 sub-regions of equal length. The force (F), line load (Q), pressure (P) and load patch aspect ratio (AR) are to be calculated with respect to the mid-length position of each sub-region (each maximum of F, Q and P is to be used in the calculation of the ice load parameters Pavg, b and w).

I2-015.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-015.text: For bow forms defined in I2.3.1(v), the shape coefficient f_ai is to be taken as f_ai = minimum(f_ai1, f_ai2, f_ai3), where f_ai1 = (0.097 - 0.68*(x/L_UI - 0.15)^2)*alpha_i/(beta_i_prime)^0.5, f_ai2 = 1.2*C_FF/(sin(beta_i_prime)*C_FC*D_UI^0.64), and f_ai3 = 0.60.

I2-017.text: (i) In the hull areas other than the bow, the force (FNonBow) and line load (QNonBow) used in the determination of the load patch dimensions (bNonBow, wNonBow) and design pressure (Pavg) are determined as follows: (a) Force, FNonBow: FNonBow = 0.36 * CFC * DF [MN] (b) Line Load, QNonBow:

I2-018.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-018.text: (i) The average pressure, Pavg, within a design load patch is determined as follows: Pavg = F / (b * w) [MPa] where F = FBow or FNonBow as appropriate for the hull area under consideration [MN] b = bBow or bNonBow as appropriate for the hull area under consideration [m] w = wBow or wNonBow as appropriate for the hull area under consideration [m] (ii) Areas of higher, concentrated pressure exist within the load patch. In general, smaller areas have higher local pressures. Accordingly, the peak pressure factors listed in Table 3 are used to account for the pressure concentration on localized structural members.

In general, smaller areas have higher local pressures. Accordingly, the peak pressure factors listed in Table 3 are used to account for the pressure concentration on localized structural members.

I2-019.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-019.text: (ii) In the event that a structural member spans across the boundary of a hull area, the largest hull area factor is to be used in the scantling determination of the member.
