I2-021.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-021.text: The required minimum shell plate thickness, t, is given by: t = tnet + ts [mm] where tnet = plate thickness required to resist ice loads according to I2.4.2 [mm] ts = corrosion and abrasion allowance according to I2.11 [mm] The thickness of shell plating required to resist the design ice load, tnet, depends on the orientation of the framing.
I2-021.normalized: The required minimum shell plate thickness, t, is given by: t = tnet + ts [mm] where tnet = plate thickness required to resist ice loads according to I2.4.2 [mm] ts = corrosion and abrasion allowance according to I2.11 [mm] The thickness of shell plating required to resist the design ice load, tnet, depends on the orientation of the framing.

I2-022.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-022.text: In the case of transversely-framed plating (Omega >= 70 deg), including all bottom plating in hull areas BI_b, M_b and S_b, the net thickness is given by t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)/(1 + s/(2*b)) [mm].
I2-022.normalized: For transversely-framed plating (Omega >= 70 deg), including bottom plating in hull areas BI_b, M_b and S_b, t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)/(1 + s/(2*b)) [mm].

I2-023.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-023.text: In the case of longitudinally-framed plating (Omega <= 20 deg), when b >= s, the net thickness is t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)/(1 + s/(2*l)) [mm]. When b < s, the net thickness is t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)*sqrt(2*b/s - (b/s)^2)/(1 + s/(2*l)) [mm].
I2-023.normalized: For longitudinally-framed plating (Omega <= 20 deg) when b >= s, t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)/(1 + s/(2*l)) [mm]. When b < s, t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)*sqrt(2*b/s - (b/s)^2)/(1 + s/(2*l)) [mm].

I2-024.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-024.text: In the case of obliquely-framed plating (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), linear interpolation is to be used.
I2-024.normalized: In the case of obliquely-framed plating (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), linear interpolation is to be used.

I2-026.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-026.text: The strength of a framing member is dependent upon the fixity that is provided at its supports. Fixity can be assumed where framing members are either continuous through the support or attached to a supporting section with a connection bracket. In other cases, simple support is to be assumed unless the connection can be demonstrated to provide significant rotational restraint. Fixity is to be ensured at the support of any framing which terminates within an ice-strengthened area.

I2-029.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-029.text: When calculating the section modulus and shear area of a framing member, net thicknesses of the web, flange (if fitted) and attached shell plating are to be used. The shear area of a framing member may include that material contained over the full depth of the member, i.e. web area including portion of flange, if fitted, but excluding attached shell plating.

I2-030.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-030.text: When the cross-sectional area of the local frame exceeds the cross-sectional area of the attached plate flange, the plastic neutral axis is z_na = (100*A_fn + h_w*t_wn - 1000*t_pn*s)/(2*t_wn) [mm], and the net effective plastic section modulus is Z_p = t_pn*s*(z_na + t_pn/2)*sin(phi_w) + (((h_w - z_na)^2 + z_na^2)*t_wn*sin(phi_w))/2000 + A_fn*((h_fc - z_na)*sin(phi_w) - b_w*cos(phi_w))/10 [cm^3]. For oblique framing (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), linear interpolation is to be used.
I2-030.normalized: When the local-frame area exceeds the attached-plate-flange area, z_na = (100*A_fn + h_w*t_wn - 1000*t_pn*s)/(2*t_wn) [mm]. The net effective plastic section modulus is Z_p = t_pn*s*(z_na + t_pn/2)*sin(phi_w) + (((h_w - z_na)^2 + z_na^2)*t_wn*sin(phi_w))/2000 + A_fn*((h_fc - z_na)*sin(phi_w) - b_w*cos(phi_w))/10 [cm^3]. For oblique framing (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), use linear interpolation.

I2-031.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-031.text: The local frames in bottom structures (i.e. hull areas BIb, Mb and Sb) and transverse local frames in side structures are to be dimensioned such that the combined effects of shear and bending do not exceed the plastic strength of the member. The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism. For bottom structure the patch load shall be applied with the dimension (b) parallel with the frame direction.

The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism. For bottom structure the patch load shall be applied with the dimension (b) parallel with the frame direction.

I2-032.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-032.text: The actual net effective shear area A_w is to comply with A_w >= A_t, where A_t = 100^2*0.5*LL*s*(AF*PPF*P_avg)/(0.577*sigma_y) [cm^2] and LL is the lesser of frame span a and load-patch height b.

I2-034.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-034.text: Longitudinal local frames in side structures are to be dimensioned such that the combined effects of shear and bending do not exceed the plastic strength of the member. The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism.

I2-035.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-035.text: The actual net effective shear area A_w is to comply with A_w >= A_L, where A_L = 100^2*(AF*PPF_s*P_avg)*0.5*b_1*a/(0.577*sigma_y) [cm^2], b_1 = k_o*b_2, k_o = 1 - 0.3/b_prime, b_prime = b/s, and b_2 = b*(1 - 0.25*b_prime) when b_prime < 2, otherwise b_2 = s.

I2-037.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-037.text: Web frames and load-carrying stringers are to be designed to withstand the ice load patch as defined in I2.3. The load patch is to be applied at locations where the capacity of these members under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised.

I2-042.normalized: (i) The flange width, bf [mm], is not to be less than five times the net thickness of the web, twn.

I2-043.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-043.text: The flange outstand is to satisfy b_out/t_fn <= 155/sqrt(sigma_y), where t_fn is the net flange thickness [mm] and sigma_y is the minimum upper yield stress [N/mm^2].
I2-043.normalized: The flange outstand shall satisfy b_out/t_fn <= 155/sqrt(sigma_y), where t_fn is the net flange thickness [mm] and sigma_y is the minimum upper yield stress [N/mm^2].

I2-046.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-046.text: Polar Class ships are to have a minimum corrosion/abrasion addition of ts = 1.0 mm applied to all internal structures within the ice-strengthened hull areas, including plated members adjacent to the shell, as well as stiffener webs and flanges.
I2-046.normalized: Polar Class ships are to have a minimum corrosion/abrasion addition of ts = 1.0 mm applied to all internal structures within the ice-strengthened hull areas, including plated members adjacent to the shell, as well as stiffener webs and flanges.

I2-047.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-047.text: Steel renewal for ice strengthened structures is required when the gauged thickness is less than tnet + 0.5 mm.
I2-047.normalized: Steel renewal for ice strengthened structures is required when the gauged thickness is less than tnet + 0.5 mm.

I2-048.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-048.text: Steel grades of plating for hull structures are to be not less than those given in Table 8 based on the as-built thickness, the Polar Class and the material class of structural members according to I2.12.2.
I2-048.normalized: Steel grades of plating for hull structures are to be not less than those given in Table 8 based on the as-built thickness, the Polar Class and the material class of structural members according to I2.12.2.

I2-050.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-050.text: The design vertical ice force at the bow is to be taken as F_IB = minimum(F_IB1, F_IB2) [MN], where F_IB1 = 0.534*K_I^0.15*sin(gamma_stem)^0.2*(D_UI*K_h)^0.5*C_FL [MN] and F_IB2 = 1.20*C_FF [MN].
I2-050.normalized: Take the design vertical ice force at the bow as F_IB = min(F_IB1, F_IB2) [MN], where F_IB1 = 0.534*K_I^0.15*sin(gamma_stem)^0.2*(D_UI*K_h)^0.5*C_FL [MN] and F_IB2 = 1.20*C_FF [MN].

I2-051.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-051.text: The design vertical ice shear force, FI, along the hull girder is to be taken as: FI = Cf * FIB [MN] where Cf = longitudinal distribution factor to be taken as follows: (a) Positive shear force Cf = 0.0 between the aft end of LUI and 0.6LUI from aft Cf = 1.0 between 0.9 LUI from aft and the forward end of LUI
I2-051.normalized: The design vertical ice shear force, FI, along the hull girder is to be taken as: FI = Cf * FIB [MN] where Cf = longitudinal distribution factor to be taken as follows: (a) Positive shear force Cf = 0.0 between the aft end of LUI and 0.6LUI from aft Cf = 1.0 between 0.9 LUI from aft and the forward end of LUI

I2-052.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-052.text: Intermediate values are to be determined by linear interpolation
I2-052.normalized: Intermediate values are to be determined by linear interpolation

I2-053.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-053.text: The applied vertical shear stress, taua, is to be determined along the hull girder in a similar manner as in UR S11.5.4.2 by substituting the design vertical ice shear force for the design vertical wave shear force.
I2-053.normalized: The applied vertical shear stress, taua, is to be determined along the hull girder in a similar manner as in UR S11.5.4.2 by substituting the design vertical ice shear force for the design vertical wave shear force.

I2-054.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-054.text: The design vertical ice bending moment along the hull girder is to be taken as M_I = 0.1*C_m*L_UI*sin(gamma_stem)^(-0.2)*F_IB [MNm]. Use C_m = 0.0 at the aft end, 1.0 between 0.5*L_UI and 0.7*L_UI from aft, 0.3 at 0.95*L_UI from aft, and 0.0 at the forward end; intermediate values are to be determined by linear interpolation.
I2-054.normalized: Take the design vertical ice bending moment along the hull girder as M_I = 0.1*C_m*L_UI*sin(gamma_stem)^(-0.2)*F_IB [MNm]. Use C_m = 0.0 at the aft end, 1.0 from 0.5*L_UI to 0.7*L_UI from aft, 0.3 at 0.95*L_UI from aft, and 0.0 at the forward end; determine intermediate values by linear interpolation.

I2-055.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-055.text: The strength criteria provided in Table 9 are to be satisfied. The design stress is not to exceed the permissible stress.
I2-055.normalized: The strength criteria provided in Table 9 are to be satisfied. The design stress is not to exceed the permissible stress.

I2-060.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-060.text: The loads carried by a member in way of cut-outs are not to cause instability. Where necessary, the structure is to be stiffened.
I2-060.normalized: The loads carried by a member in way of cut-outs are not to cause instability. Where necessary, the structure is to be stiffened.

I2-061.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-061.text: Direct calculations are not to be utilised as an alternative to the analytical procedures prescribed for the shell plating and local frame requirements given in I2.4, I2.6, and I2.7.
I2-061.normalized: Direct calculations are not to be utilised as an alternative to the analytical procedures prescribed for the shell plating and local frame requirements given in I2.4, I2.6, and I2.7.

I2-062.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-062.text: Direct calculations are to be used for load carrying stringers and web frames forming part of a grillage system.
I2-062.normalized: Direct calculations are to be used for load carrying stringers and web frames forming part of a grillage system.

I2-064.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-064.text: For linear calculation methods: web plates and flange elements in compression and shear are to fulfil the relevant buckling criteria specified by the Classification Society; nominal shear stress in member web plates is to be less than sigma_y/sqrt(3); and nominal von Mises stress in member flanges is to be less than 1.15*sigma_y.
I2-064.normalized: For linear structural calculations: web plates and flange elements in compression and shear shall meet the applicable buckling criteria; nominal shear stress in member webs shall be less than sigma_y/sqrt(3); and nominal von Mises stress in member flanges shall be less than 1.15*sigma_y.

I2-065.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-065.text: If the structure is evaluated based on non-linear calculation methods, the following are to be considered: (1) The analysis is to reliably capture buckling and plastic deformation of the structure (2) The acceptance criteria are to ensure a suitable margin against fracture and major buckling and yielding causing significant loss of stiffness (3) Permanent lateral and out-of plane deformation of considered member are to be minor relative to the relevant structural dimensions
I2-065.normalized: If the structure is evaluated based on non-linear calculation methods, the following are to be considered: (1) The analysis is to reliably capture buckling and plastic deformation of the structure (2) The acceptance criteria are to ensure a suitable margin against fracture and major buckling and yielding causing significant loss of stiffness (3) Permanent lateral and out-of plane deformation of considered member are to be minor relative to the relevant structural dimensions

I2-066.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-066.text: All welding within ice-strengthened areas is to be of the double continuous type.
I2-066.normalized: All welding within ice-strengthened areas is to be of the double continuous type.

I2-067.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
I2-067.text: Continuity of strength is to be ensured at all structural connections.
I2-067.normalized: Continuity of strength is to be ensured at all structural connections.

IMO-001.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-001.text: Category A ship means a ship designed for operation in polar waters in at least medium first-year ice, which may include old ice inclusions.
IMO-001.normalized: IF a ship is designed to operate in at least medium first-year ice, including possible old-ice inclusions, THEN ship_category = 'A'.

IMO-002.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-002.text: Category B ship means a ship not included in category A, designed for operation in polar waters in at least thin first-year ice, which may include old ice inclusions.
IMO-002.normalized: IF a ship is not category A and is designed to operate in at least thin first-year ice, including possible old-ice inclusions, THEN ship_category = 'B'.

IMO-003.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-003.text: Category C ship means a ship designed to operate in open water or in ice conditions less severe than those included in categories A and B.
IMO-003.normalized: IF a ship is designed for open water or ice conditions less severe than categories A and B, THEN ship_category = 'C'.

IMO-004.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-004.text: First-year ice means sea ice of not more than one winter growth developing from young ice with thickness from 0.3 m to 2.0 m.
IMO-004.normalized: IF ice_origin = 'sea ice' AND winter_growth_count <= 1 AND 0.3 <= ice_thickness_m <= 2.0, THEN ice_type = 'first-year ice'.

IMO-005.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-005.text: Ice free waters means no ice present. If ice of any kind is present this term shall not be used.
IMO-005.normalized: ice_condition = 'ice free waters' ONLY IF total_ice_present = false.

IMO-006.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-006.text: Medium first-year ice means first-year ice of 0.7 m to 1.2 m thickness.
IMO-006.normalized: IF ice_type = 'medium first-year ice', THEN 0.7 <= ice_thickness_m <= 1.2.

IMO-007.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-007.text: Open water means a large area of freely navigable water in which sea ice is present in concentrations less than 1/10. No ice of land origin is present.
IMO-007.normalized: IF ice_condition = 'open water', THEN sea_ice_concentration_tenths < 1 AND ice_of_land_origin_present = false.

IMO-008.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-008.text: Thin first-year ice means first-year ice of 0.3 m to 0.7 m thickness.
IMO-008.normalized: IF ice_type = 'thin first-year ice', THEN 0.3 <= ice_thickness_m <= 0.7.

IMO-009.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-009.text: Bergy waters mean an area of freely navigable water in which ice of land origin is present in concentrations less than 1/10. There may be sea ice present, although the total concentration of all ice shall not exceed 1/10.
IMO-009.normalized: IF ice_condition = 'bergy waters', THEN land_origin_ice_concentration_tenths < 1 AND total_ice_concentration_tenths <= 1.

IMO-010.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-010.text: Maximum expected time of rescue means the time adopted for the design of equipment and system that provide survival support. It shall never be less than 5 days.

IMO-011.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-011.text: Mean Daily Low Temperature (MDLT) means the mean value of the daily low temperature for each day of the year over a minimum 10 year period. A data set acceptable to the Administration may be used if 10 years of data is not available.
IMO-011.normalized: MDLT_degC shall be calculated from daily low temperatures over data_period_years >= 10; if data_period_years < 10, administration_dataset_approval_status shall be valid.

IMO-012.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-012.text: Polar Service Temperature (PST) means a temperature specified for a ship which is intended to operate in low air temperature, which shall be set at least 10 deg C below the lowest MDLT for the intended area and season of operation in polar waters.

IMO-013.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-013.text: Ship intended to operate in low air temperature means a ship which is intended to undertake voyages to or through areas where the lowest Mean Daily Low Temperature (MDLT) is below -10 deg C.

IMO-014.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-014.text: Every ship to which this Code applies shall have on board a valid Polar Ship Certificate.
IMO-014.normalized: IF polar_code_applies = true, THEN polar_ship_certificate_present = true AND polar_ship_certificate_status = valid.
IMO-014.verification_mode: Conditional document presence and status constraint

IMO-015.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-015.text: Except as provided for in paragraph 1.3.3, the Polar Ship Certificate shall be issued after an initial or renewal survey to a ship which complies with the relevant requirements of this Code.
IMO-015.normalized: Except where clause 1.3.3 applies, certificate_issued = true ONLY IF qualifying_survey_type is initial or renewal AND survey_compliance_status = passed.

IMO-016.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-016.text: The Polar Ship Certificate shall be drawn up in a form corresponding to the model given in appendix I to this Code. If the language used is neither English, nor French or Spanish, the text shall include a translation into one of these languages.
IMO-016.normalized: polar_ship_certificate_form = 'Appendix I model'; IF certificate_language NOT IN {'English','French','Spanish'}, THEN approved_translation_present = true.
IMO-016.verification_mode: Document template and conditional language constraint

IMO-017.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-017.text: Polar Ship Certificate validity, survey dates and endorsements shall be harmonized with the relevant SOLAS certificates in accordance with the provisions of SOLAS regulation I/14. The certificate shall include a supplement, recording equipment required by the Code.
IMO-017.normalized: The Polar Ship Certificate validity dates, survey dates, and endorsements shall match the applicable SOLAS certificate schedule, and polar_certificate_supplement_present shall be true with required equipment records.

IMO-018.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-018.text: Where applicable, the certificate shall reference a methodology to assess operational capabilities and limitations in ice to the satisfaction of the Administration, taking into account the guidelines developed by the Organization.
IMO-018.normalized: IF ice_capability_methodology_applicable = true, THEN certificate_methodology_reference_present = true AND administration_acceptance_status = approved.

IMO-019.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-019.text: For ships operating in low air temperature, a Polar Service Temperature (PST) shall be specified and shall be at least 10 deg C below the lowest MDLT for the intended area and season of operation in polar waters. Systems and equipment required by this Code shall be fully functional at the PST.
IMO-019.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN PST_degC shall be specified, PST_degC <= lowest_MDLT_degC - 10, and required_systems_functional_at_PST = true.

IMO-020.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-020.text: For ships operating in low air temperature, survival systems and equipment shall be fully operational at the PST during the maximum expected rescue time.
IMO-020.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN survival_system_test_temperature_degC <= PST_degC AND demonstrated_operating_duration_days >= maximum_expected_rescue_time_days AND survival_system_test_status = passed.

IMO-021.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-021.text: In order to establish procedures or operational limitations, an assessment of the ship and its equipment shall be carried out, taking into consideration the following: the anticipated range of operating and environmental conditions, such as operation in low air temperature, operation in ice, operation in high latitude, and potential for abandonment onto ice or land; hazards, as listed in section 3 of the Introduction, as applicable; and additional hazards, if identified.
IMO-021.normalized: An operational assessment shall exist and cover low-air-temperature operation, ice operation, high-latitude operation, abandonment onto ice or land, applicable Introduction section 3 hazards, and any identified additional hazards.

IMO-022.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-022.text: The Manual shall include information on the ship-specific capabilities and limitations in relation to the assessment required under paragraph 1.5.
IMO-022.normalized: PWOM shall include ship-specific capabilities and limitations linked to the clause 1.5 operational assessment.

IMO-023.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-023.text: The Manual shall include or refer to specific procedures to be followed in normal operations and in order to avoid encountering conditions that exceed the ship's capabilities.
IMO-023.normalized: PWOM shall include or reference procedures for normal operations and avoidance of conditions exceeding ship capabilities.

IMO-024.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-024.text: The Manual shall include or refer to specific procedures to be followed in the event of incidents in polar waters.
IMO-024.normalized: PWOM shall include or reference polar-water incident procedures.

IMO-025.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-025.text: In order to comply with the functional requirements in section 2.2, the Manual shall be carried on board.

IMO-026.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-026.text: In order to comply with the functional requirements of paragraph 2.2.2, the Manual shall contain, where applicable, the methodology used to determine capabilities and limitations in ice.
IMO-026.normalized: IF ice_capability_methodology_applicable = true, THEN PWOM_ice_capability_methodology_present = true.

IMO-027.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-027.text: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures for the following: voyage planning to avoid ice and/or temperatures that exceed the ship's design capabilities or limitations; arrangements for receiving forecasts of the environmental conditions; means of addressing any limitations of the hydrographic, meteorological and navigational information available; operation of equipment required under other chapters of this Code; and implementation of special measures to maintain equipment and system functionality under low temperatures, topside icing and the presence of sea ice, as applicable.
IMO-027.normalized: PWOM shall include risk-based procedures covering voyage-limit avoidance, environmental forecasts, information limitations, required-equipment operation, and applicable low-temperature, topside-icing, and sea-ice functionality measures.

IMO-028.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-028.text: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures to be followed for: contacting emergency response providers for salvage, search and rescue (SAR), spill response, etc., as applicable; and, in the case of ships ice strengthened in accordance with chapter 3, procedures for maintaining life support and ship integrity in the event of prolonged entrapment by ice.
IMO-028.normalized: PWOM shall include applicable emergency-provider contact procedures; IF ship_ice_strengthened = true, THEN PWOM shall also include prolonged-ice-entrapment life-support and integrity procedures.

IMO-029.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-029.text: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures to be followed for measures to be taken in the event of encountering ice and/or temperatures which exceed the ship's design capabilities or limitations.
IMO-029.normalized: PWOM shall include procedures for encounters with ice or temperatures exceeding ship design capabilities or limitations.

IMO-030.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-030.text: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures for monitoring and maintaining safety during operations in ice, as applicable, including any requirements for escort operations or icebreaker assistance. Different operational limitations may apply depending on whether the ship is operating independently or with icebreaker escort. Where appropriate, the PWOM should specify both options.
IMO-030.normalized: IF ice_operation_applicable = true, THEN PWOM shall include ice-operation monitoring and safety procedures, including applicable escort or icebreaker-assistance requirements and operating-mode-specific limitations.

IMO-031.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-031.text: Materials of exposed structures in ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety based on the polar service temperature.
IMO-031.normalized: Every exposed-structure material shall have approval evidence from the Administration or an accepted recognized organization, and the approval basis shall reference the PST and an accepted or equivalent-safety standard.

IMO-032.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-032.text: Scantlings of category A ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety; scantlings of category B ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety; and scantlings of ice strengthened category C ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account acceptable standards adequate for the ice types and concentrations encountered in the area of operation.
IMO-032.normalized: For category A, category B, and ice-strengthened category C ships, scantling_approval_status shall be approved by the Administration or an accepted recognized organization; the approval standard shall be accepted or provide equivalent safety, and category C approval shall address operating-area ice type and concentration.

IMO-033.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-033.text: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations: 30 kg/m^2 on exposed weather decks and gangways; 7.5 kg/m^2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the water plane; and the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms, spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this area by 10%.
IMO-033.normalized: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN deck_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 30, side_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 7.5, discontinuous_surface_projected_area = continuous_surface_projected_area * 1.05, and discontinuous_surface_static_moment = continuous_surface_static_moment * 1.10.

IMO-034.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-034.text: Ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur shall be: designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and erections.
IMO-034.normalized: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN ice_accretion_minimization_design_present = true AND required_ice_removal_means_present = true.

IMO-035.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-035.text: Information on the icing allowance included in the stability calculations shall be given in the PWOM.
IMO-035.normalized: PWOM_icing_allowance_information_present = true AND PWOM_icing_allowance_values shall match the stability calculation.

IMO-036.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-036.text: Ice accretion shall be monitored and appropriate measures taken to ensure that the ice accretion does not exceed the values given in the PWOM.
IMO-036.normalized: ice_accretion_monitoring_active = true; for every monitoring observation, observed_ice_accretion <= PWOM_ice_accretion_limit, or a linked corrective_action_status shall show action taken.

IMO-037.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-037.text: Ships of categories A and B, constructed on or after 1 January 2017, shall be able to withstand flooding resulting from hull penetration due to ice impact. The residual stability following ice damage shall be such that the factor s_i, as defined in SOLAS regulations II-1/7-2.2 and II-1/7-2.3, is equal to one for all loading conditions used to calculate the attained subdivision index in SOLAS regulation II-1/7. However, for cargo ships that comply with subdivision and damage stability regulations in another instrument developed by the Organization, as provided by SOLAS regulation II-1/4.1, the residual stability criteria of that instrument shall be met for each loading condition.
IMO-037.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN for every applicable loading condition either residual_stability_factor_s_i = 1 or, where the SOLAS II-1/4.1 alternative applies, alternative_instrument_residual_stability_status = compliant.

IMO-038.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-038.text: The ice damage extents to be assumed when demonstrating compliance with paragraph 4.3.2.1 shall be such that: the longitudinal extent is 4.5% of the upper ice waterline length if centred forward of the maximum breadth on the upper ice waterline, and 1.5% of upper ice waterline length otherwise, and shall be assumed at any longitudinal position along the ship's length; the transverse penetration extent is 760 mm, measured normal to the shell over the full extent of the damage; and the vertical extent is the lesser of 20% of the upper ice waterline draught or the longitudinal extent, and shall be assumed at any vertical position between the keel and 120% of the upper ice waterline draught.
IMO-038.normalized: longitudinal_damage_extent = 0.045 * upper_ice_waterline_length when damage_center_forward_of_max_breadth = true, otherwise 0.015 * upper_ice_waterline_length; transverse_penetration_mm = 760; vertical_damage_extent = min(0.20 * upper_ice_waterline_draught, longitudinal_damage_extent); allowed_vertical_position is between keel and 1.20 * upper_ice_waterline_draught.

IMO-039.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-039.text: All closing appliances and doors relevant to watertight and weathertight integrity of the ship shall be operable.

IMO-040.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-040.text: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, means shall be provided to remove or prevent ice and snow accretion around hatches and doors.
IMO-040.normalized: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN every relevant hatch and door shall have an associated ice_or_snow_removal_or_prevention_means.

IMO-041.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-041.text: If the hatches or doors are hydraulically operated, means shall be provided to prevent freezing or excessive viscosity of liquids.

IMO-042.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-042.text: Watertight and weathertight doors, hatches and closing devices which are not within an habitable environment and require access while at sea shall be designed to be operated by personnel wearing heavy winter clothing including thick mittens.
IMO-042.normalized: IF closing_device_outside_habitable_environment = true AND access_required_at_sea = true, THEN winter_clothing_operability_test_status = passed, including operation with thick mittens.

IMO-043.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-043.text: Machinery installations and associated equipment shall be protected against the effect of ice accretion and/or snow accumulation, ice ingestion from sea water, freezing and increased viscosity of liquids, seawater intake temperature and snow ingestion.
IMO-043.normalized: Every machinery installation and associated equipment shall have protection coverage for applicable ice accretion, snow accumulation, seawater ice ingestion, liquid freezing or viscosity increase, seawater intake temperature, and snow ingestion hazards.

IMO-044.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-044.text: Working liquids shall be maintained in a viscosity range that ensures operation of the machinery.
IMO-044.normalized: For every time-stamped working-liquid observation, manufacturer_min_viscosity <= observed_viscosity <= manufacturer_max_viscosity.

IMO-045.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-045.text: Seawater supplies for machinery systems shall be designed to prevent ingestion of ice, or otherwise arranged to ensure functionality.
IMO-045.normalized: Every machinery seawater supply shall have ice_ingestion_prevention_present = true OR alternate_functionality_arrangement_approval_status = approved.

IMO-046.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-046.text: For ships intended to operate in low air temperatures, exposed machinery and electrical installation and appliances shall function at the PST.
IMO-046.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every exposed machinery item, electrical installation, and appliance shall have functional_test_temperature_degC <= PST_degC AND functional_test_status = passed.

IMO-047.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-047.text: Means shall be provided to ensure that combustion air for internal combustion engines driving essential machinery is maintained at a temperature in compliance with the criteria provided by the engine manufacturer.
IMO-047.normalized: For every internal combustion engine driving essential machinery, combustion_air_temperature_control_present = true AND combustion_air_temperature_degC shall be within the engine manufacturer criteria.
IMO-047.verification_mode: Qualified equipment and numeric range constraint

IMO-048.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-048.text: Materials of exposed machinery and foundations shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety based on the PST.
IMO-048.normalized: Every exposed machinery or foundation material shall have approval evidence from an accepted authority based on PST and an accepted or equivalent-safety standard.

IMO-049.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-049.text: Scantlings of propeller blades, propulsion line, steering equipment and other appendages of category A ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety; scantlings of propeller blades, propulsion line, steering equipment and other appendages of category B ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety; and scantlings of propeller blades, propulsion line, steering equipment and other appendages of ice-strengthened category C ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account acceptable standards adequate with the ice types and concentration encountered in the area of operation.
IMO-049.normalized: For category A, category B, and ice-strengthened category C ships, each propeller blade, propulsion-line, steering-equipment, and appendage scantling shall have approval evidence from an accepted authority using an accepted or equivalent-safety standard; category C evidence shall address operating ice type and concentration.

IMO-050.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-050.text: All components of fire safety systems and appliances if installed in exposed positions shall be protected from ice accretion and snow accumulation.
IMO-050.normalized: IF fire_safety_component_exposed = true, THEN ice_and_snow_protection_present = true.

IMO-051.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-051.text: Local equipment and machinery controls shall be arranged so as to avoid freezing, snow accumulation and ice accretion and their location to remain accessible at all time.
IMO-051.normalized: Every local equipment or machinery control shall have freezing_snow_ice_protection_present = true AND continuously_accessible = true.

IMO-052.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-052.text: Means shall be provided to remove or prevent ice and snow accretion from accesses.
IMO-052.normalized: Every required access shall have an associated ice_or_snow_removal_or_prevention_means.

IMO-053.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-053.text: Extinguishing media shall be suitable for intended operation.
IMO-053.normalized: Every extinguishing medium shall have intended_operation_compatibility_status = approved.

IMO-054.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-054.text: All components of fire safety systems and appliances shall be designed to ensure availability and effectiveness at the PST.
IMO-054.normalized: For every fire-safety component, PST_availability_effectiveness_test_temperature_degC <= PST_degC AND PST_test_status = passed.

IMO-055.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-055.text: Isolating and pressure/vacuum valves in exposed locations shall be protected from ice accretion and remain accessible at all times.
IMO-055.normalized: IF valve_exposed = true AND valve_type IN {isolating, pressure, vacuum}, THEN ice_accretion_protection_present = true AND continuously_accessible = true.

IMO-056.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-056.text: All two-way portable radio communication equipment shall be operable at the PST.
IMO-056.normalized: For every two-way portable radio, operating_test_temperature_degC <= PST_degC AND operating_test_status = passed.

IMO-057.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-057.text: Fire pumps, including emergency fire pumps, water mist and water spray pumps, shall be located in compartments maintained above freezing.
IMO-057.normalized: Every fire pump, emergency fire pump, water-mist pump, and water-spray pump shall be located in a compartment with maintained_temperature_degC > 0.

IMO-058.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-058.text: The fire main is to be arranged so that exposed sections can be isolated and means of draining of exposed sections shall be provided.
IMO-058.normalized: Every exposed fire-main section shall have isolation_capability = true AND drainage_means_present = true.

IMO-059.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-059.text: Firefighter's outfits shall be stored in warm locations on the ship.
IMO-059.normalized: Every firefighter_outfit shall be stored in a location classified as warm.

IMO-060.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-060.text: Where fixed water-based firefighting systems are located in a space separate from the main fire pumps and use their own independent sea suction, this sea suction shall also be capable of being cleared of ice accumulation.
IMO-060.normalized: IF fixed_water_system_separate_from_main_fire_pumps = true AND independent_sea_suction_used = true, THEN sea_suction_ice_clearing_capability = true.

IMO-061.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-061.text: Portable and semi-portable extinguishers shall be located in positions protected from freezing temperatures, as far as practical. Locations subject to freezing are to be provided with extinguishers capable of operation at the PST.
IMO-061.normalized: Every portable or semi-portable extinguisher shall be in a freezing-protected location; IF storage_location_subject_to_freezing = true, THEN extinguisher_operating_test_temperature_degC <= PST_degC AND operating_test_status = passed.
IMO-061.verification_mode: Conditional location and environmental test constraint

IMO-062.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-062.text: Exposed escape routes shall remain accessible and safe, taking into consideration the potential icing of structures and snow accumulation.
IMO-062.normalized: Every exposed escape route shall have accessible_status = true, safe_status = true, and documented ice/snow mitigation coverage.

IMO-063.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-063.text: All life-saving appliances and associated equipment shall provide safe evacuation and be functional under the possible adverse environmental conditions during the maximum expected time of rescue.
IMO-063.normalized: Every life-saving appliance and associated equipment item shall have evacuation_test_status = passed under applicable adverse conditions for demonstrated_duration_days >= maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.

IMO-064.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-064.text: Adequate thermal protection shall be provided for all persons on board, taking into account the intended voyage, the anticipated weather conditions (cold and wind) and the potential for immersion in polar water, where applicable.
IMO-064.normalized: Every person on board shall have assigned thermal-protection equipment supported by an adequacy approval covering intended voyage, anticipated cold and wind, and applicable polar-water immersion.

IMO-065.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-065.text: Taking into account the presence of any hazards, as identified in the assessment in chapter 1, resources shall be provided to support survival following abandoning ship, whether to the water, to ice or to land, for the maximum expected time of rescue. These resources shall provide: a habitable environment; protection of persons from the effects of cold, wind and sun; space to accommodate persons equipped with thermal protection adequate for the environment; means to provide sustenance; safe access and exit points; and means to communicate with rescue assets.
IMO-065.normalized: Survival resources shall support the assessed abandonment environments for at least maximum_expected_rescue_time_days and shall cover habitable environment, cold/wind/sun protection, accommodation space, sustenance, safe access/exit, and rescue communication.

IMO-066.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-066.text: For ships exposed to ice accretion, means shall be provided to remove or prevent ice and snow accretion from escape routes, muster stations, embarkation areas, survival craft, their launching appliances and access to survival craft.
IMO-066.normalized: IF ship_exposed_to_ice_accretion = true, THEN every escape route, muster station, embarkation area, survival craft, launching appliance, and survival-craft access shall have an associated ice_or_snow_removal_or_prevention_means.

IMO-067.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-067.text: For ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, exposed escape routes shall be arranged so as not to hinder passage by persons wearing suitable polar clothing.
IMO-067.normalized: IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN every exposed escape route shall have polar_clothing_passage_test_status = passed.

IMO-068.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-068.text: Ships shall have means to ensure safe evacuation of persons, including safe deployment of survival equipment, when operating in ice-covered waters, or directly onto the ice, as applicable.
IMO-068.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_ice_covered_waters = true OR direct_evacuation_onto_ice_applicable = true, THEN safe_evacuation_means_present = true AND survival_equipment_deployment_approval_status = approved.

IMO-069.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-069.text: Where the regulations of this chapter are achieved by means of adding devices requiring a source of power, this source shall be able to operate independently of the ship's main source of power.

IMO-070.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-070.text: For passenger ships, a proper sized immersion suit or a thermal protective aid shall be provided for each person on board.
IMO-070.normalized: IF ship_type = passenger_ship, THEN every person on board shall have one properly sized immersion suit OR one thermal protective aid.

IMO-071.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-071.text: Where immersion suits are required, they shall be of the insulated type.
IMO-071.normalized: IF immersion_suit_required = true, THEN immersion_suit_type = insulated.

IMO-072.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-072.text: For ships intended to operate in extended periods of darkness, searchlights suitable for continuous use to facilitate identification of ice shall be provided for each lifeboat.
IMO-072.normalized: IF extended_darkness_operation = true, THEN every lifeboat shall have an assigned searchlight with continuous_use_suitability_status = approved.

IMO-073.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-073.text: No lifeboat shall be of any type other than partially or totally enclosed.
IMO-073.normalized: Every lifeboat_type shall be in {'partially enclosed','totally enclosed'}.

IMO-074.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-074.text: Whenever the assessment identifies a potential of abandonment onto ice or land, group survival equipment shall be carried, unless an equivalent level of functionality for survival is provided by the ship's normal life-saving appliances.
IMO-074.normalized: IF abandonment_onto_ice_or_land_potential = true, THEN group_survival_equipment_carried = true OR normal_life_saving_equivalent_functionality_approval_status = approved.

IMO-075.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-075.text: When required, personal and group survival equipment sufficient for 110% of the persons on board shall be stowed in easily accessible locations, as close as practical to the muster or embarkation stations.
IMO-075.normalized: IF personal_or_group_survival_equipment_required = true, THEN available_survival_equipment_capacity >= ceil(persons_on_board * 1.10) AND storage_accessibility_status = accessible.

IMO-076.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-076.text: Containers for group survival equipment shall be designed to be easily movable over the ice and be floatable.
IMO-076.normalized: Every group-survival-equipment container shall have ice_mobility_test_status = passed AND flotation_test_status = passed.

IMO-077.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-077.text: If carried in addition to persons, in the survival craft, the survival craft and launching appliances shall have sufficient capacity to accommodate the additional equipment.
IMO-077.normalized: IF additional_equipment_carried_in_survival_craft = true, THEN survival_craft_available_capacity >= persons_capacity_requirement + additional_equipment_capacity_requirement AND launching_appliance_capacity >= loaded_survival_craft_requirement.

IMO-078.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-078.text: Passengers shall be instructed in the use of the personal survival equipment and the action to take in an emergency; and the crew shall be trained in the use of the personal survival equipment and group survival equipment.
IMO-078.normalized: Every passenger shall have personal-survival-equipment instruction_status = completed; every crew member shall have personal_and_group_survival_equipment_training_status = completed.

IMO-079.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-079.text: Adequate emergency rations shall be provided, for the maximum expected time of rescue.

IMO-080.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-080.text: Ships shall have means of receiving and displaying current information on ice conditions in the area of operation.
IMO-080.normalized: ice_information_receiver_present = true AND ice_information_display_present = true AND displayed_ice_information_status = current for the operating area.

IMO-081.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-081.text: Ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, ice strengthened in accordance with chapter 3, shall have either two independent echo-sounding devices or one echo-sounding device with two separate independent transducers.
IMO-081.normalized: IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND ship_ice_strengthened = true, THEN independent_echo_sounding_device_count >= 2 OR (echo_sounding_device_count >= 1 AND independent_transducer_count >= 2).

IMO-082.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-082.text: Ships shall comply with SOLAS regulation V/22.1.9.4, irrespective of the date of construction and the size and, depending on the bridge configuration, have a clear view astern.
IMO-082.normalized: SOLAS_V_22_1_9_4_compliance_status = compliant AND, where required by bridge configuration, clear_view_astern_status = compliant.
IMO-082.verification_mode: Cross-regulation compliance and conditional status constraint

IMO-083.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-083.text: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, means to prevent the accumulation of ice on antennas required for navigation and communication shall be provided.
IMO-083.normalized: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN every required navigation or communication antenna shall have ice_accumulation_prevention_means_present = true.

IMO-084.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-084.text: Where equipment required by SOLAS chapter V or this chapter has sensors that project below the hull, such sensors shall be protected against ice.
IMO-084.normalized: IF required_sensor_projects_below_hull = true, THEN sensor_ice_protection_present = true.

IMO-085.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-085.text: In category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, the bridge wings shall be enclosed or designed to protect navigational equipment and operating personnel.
IMO-085.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN bridge_wings_enclosed = true OR bridge_wing_protection_design_status = approved.

IMO-086.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-086.text: Ships shall have two non-magnetic means to determine and display their heading. Both means shall be independent and shall be connected to the ship's main and emergency source of power.
IMO-086.normalized: non_magnetic_heading_means_count >= 2; the two means shall be independent and each shall be connected to main_power and emergency_power.

IMO-087.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-087.text: Ships proceeding to latitudes over 80 degrees shall be fitted with at least one GNSS compass or equivalent, which shall be connected to the ship's main and emergency source of power.
IMO-087.normalized: IF planned_or_actual_latitude_deg > 80, THEN GNSS_compass_or_equivalent_count >= 1 AND connected_to_main_power = true AND connected_to_emergency_power = true.

IMO-088.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-088.text: Ships, with the exception of those solely operating in areas with 24 h daylight, shall be equipped with two remotely rotatable, narrow-beam search lights controllable from the bridge to provide lighting over an arc of 360 degrees, or other means to visually detect ice.
IMO-088.normalized: IF solely_24_hour_daylight_operation = false, THEN (bridge_controlled_rotatable_narrow_beam_searchlight_count >= 2 AND searchlight_coverage_arc_deg >= 360) OR alternate_visual_ice_detection_means_approval_status = approved.

IMO-089.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-089.text: Ships involved in operations with an icebreaker escort shall be equipped with a manually initiated flashing red light visible from astern to indicate when the ship is stopped. This light shall have a range of visibility of at least two nautical miles, and the horizontal and vertical arcs of visibility shall conform to the stern light specifications required by the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.
IMO-089.normalized: IF icebreaker_escort_operation = true, THEN manually_initiated_flashing_red_stopped_light_present = true, light_visible_from_astern = true, visibility_range_nm >= 2, and COLREG_stern_light_arc_compliance_status = compliant.

IMO-090.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-090.text: Two-way voice and/or data communications ship-to-ship and ship-to-shore shall be available at all points along the intended operating routes.
IMO-090.normalized: For every point on the intended operating route, ship_to_ship_communication_available = true AND ship_to_shore_communication_available = true using voice and/or data.

IMO-091.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-091.text: Means for two-way on-scene and SAR coordination communications for search and rescue purposes including aeronautical frequencies shall be provided.
IMO-091.normalized: two_way_on_scene_communication_present = true AND SAR_coordination_communication_present = true AND aeronautical_frequency_capability_present = true.

IMO-092.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-092.text: Appropriate communication equipment to enable telemedical assistance in polar areas shall be provided.

IMO-093.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-093.text: Mandatory communication equipment for use in survival craft, including liferafts and rescue boats, shall be capable of operation during the maximum expected time of rescue.
IMO-093.normalized: Every mandatory survival-craft communication device shall have demonstrated_operating_duration_days >= maximum_expected_rescue_time_days AND duration_test_status = passed.

IMO-094.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-094.text: Ships intended to provide icebreaking escort shall be equipped with a sound signaling system mounted to face astern to indicate escort and emergency manoeuvres to following ships as described in the International Code of Signals.
IMO-094.normalized: IF ship_provides_icebreaking_escort = true, THEN astern_facing_sound_signaling_system_present = true AND International_Code_of_Signals_compliance_status = compliant.

IMO-095.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-095.text: Two-way on-scene and SAR coordination communication capability in ships shall include: voice and/or data communications with relevant rescue coordination centres; and equipment for voice communications with aircraft on 121.5 and 123.1 MHz.
IMO-095.normalized: SAR_communication_capability shall include rescue_coordination_centre_voice_or_data = true AND aircraft_voice_frequency_support_MHz containing both 121.5 and 123.1.

IMO-096.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-096.text: The communication equipment shall provide for two-way voice and data communication with a Telemedical Assistance Service (TMAS).

IMO-097.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-097.text: For ships intended to operate in low air temperature, all rescue boats and lifeboats, whenever released for evacuation, shall: for distress alerting, carry one device for transmitting ship-to-shore alerts; in order to be located, carry one device for transmitting signals for location; and for on-scene communications, carry one device for transmitting and receiving on-scene communications.
IMO-097.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every released rescue boat and lifeboat shall carry at least one ship-to-shore distress-alert device, one location-signal device, and one on-scene transmit/receive communication device.

IMO-098.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-098.text: For ships intended to operate in low air temperature, all other survival craft shall: in order to be located, carry one device for transmitting signals for location; and for on-scene communications, carry one device for transmitting and receiving on-scene communications.
IMO-098.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every other survival craft shall carry at least one location-signal device and one on-scene transmit/receive communication device.

IMO-099.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-099.text: Recognizing the limitations arising from battery life, procedures shall be developed and implemented such that mandatory communication equipment for use in survival craft, including liferafts and rescue boats, are available for operation during the maximum expected time of rescue.
IMO-099.normalized: battery_life_management_procedure_present = true AND procedure_implementation_status = active AND every mandatory survival-craft communication device shall remain available for maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.

IMO-100.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-100.text: The voyage plan shall take into account the potential hazards of the intended voyage.
IMO-100.normalized: voyage_plan_present = true AND every identified_intended_voyage_hazard shall be addressed by the voyage plan.

IMO-101.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-101.text: The master shall consider a route through polar waters, taking into account the following: the procedures required by the PWOM; any limitations of the hydrographic information and aids to navigation available; current information on the extent and type of ice and icebergs in the vicinity of the intended route; statistical information on ice and temperatures from former years; places of refuge; current information and measures to be taken when marine mammals are encountered, relating to known areas with densities of marine mammals, including seasonal migration areas; current information on relevant ships' routing systems, speed recommendations and vessel traffic services relating to known areas with densities of marine mammals, including seasonal migration areas; national and international designated protected areas along the route; and operation in areas remote from SAR capabilities.
IMO-101.normalized: The polar-route planning record shall cover all nine clause 11.3 topics: PWOM procedures, hydrographic/navigation limitations, current ice/iceberg information, historical ice/temperature data, places of refuge, marine-mammal measures, routing/speed/VTS information, protected areas, and remoteness from SAR.

IMO-102.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-102.text: In order to meet the functional requirement of paragraph 12.2 above while operating in polar waters, masters, chief mates and officers in charge of a navigational watch shall be qualified in accordance with chapter V of the STCW Convention and the STCW Code, as amended, as follows: Ice conditions | Tankers | Passenger ships | Other. Ice free | Not applicable. | Not applicable. | Not applicable. Open waters | Basic training for master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Basic training for master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Not applicable. Other waters | Advanced training for master and chief mate. Basic training for officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Advanced training for master and chief mate. Basic training for officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Advanced training for master and chief mate. Basic training for officers in charge of a navigational watch.
IMO-102.normalized: Required polar training level shall be derived from ice_condition, ship_type, and crew_role according to the clause 12.3.1 matrix, and each applicable crew member shall have a valid matching STCW qualification.

IMO-103.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-103.text: The Administration may allow the use of a person(s) other than the master, chief mate or officers of the navigational watch to satisfy the requirements for training, provided that: this person(s) shall be qualified and certified in accordance with regulation II/2 of the STCW Convention and section A-II/2 of the STCW Code, and meet the advance training requirements set out in the table in paragraph 12.3.1; while operating in polar waters the ship carries a sufficient number of persons meeting the appropriate training requirements for polar waters to cover all watches; this person(s) is subject to the Administration's minimum hours of rest requirements at all times; when operating in waters other than open waters or bergy waters, the master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch on passenger ships and tankers shall meet the applicable basic training requirements set out in the table in paragraph 12.3.1; and when operating in waters with an ice concentration of more than 2/10, the master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch on cargo ships other than tankers shall meet the applicable basic training requirements set out in the table in paragraph 12.3.1.
IMO-103.normalized: IF alternate_qualified_person_used = true, THEN administration_permission_status = approved and all five conditions in clause 12.3.2 shall be satisfied, including STCW II/2 and A-II/2 certification, advanced polar training, watch coverage, rest compliance, and the condition-specific basic-training safeguards for designated officers.

IMO-104.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-104.text: Every crew member shall be made familiar with the procedures and equipment contained or referenced in the PWOM relevant to their assigned duties.
IMO-104.normalized: Every crew member shall have PWOM_familiarization_status = completed for all procedures and equipment relevant to assigned_duties.

IMO-105.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-105.text: In Arctic waters any discharge into the sea of oil or oily mixtures from any ship shall be prohibited.
IMO-105.normalized: IF operating_area = Arctic_waters, THEN oil_or_oily_mixture_discharge_to_sea = false.

IMO-106.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-106.text: The provisions of paragraph 1.1.1 shall not apply to the discharge of clean or segregated ballast.
IMO-106.normalized: IF discharged_material_type IN {clean_ballast, segregated_ballast}, THEN clause_1_1_1_oil_discharge_prohibition_applicable = false.

IMO-107.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-107.text: Operation in polar waters shall be taken into account, as appropriate, in the Oil Record Books, manuals and the shipboard oil pollution emergency plan or the shipboard marine pollution emergency plan as required by MARPOL Annex I.
IMO-107.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN polar_operation_coverage shall be present in the applicable Oil Record Book, manuals, and oil or marine pollution emergency plan.

IMO-108.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-108.text: For category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017 with an aggregate oil fuel capacity of less than 600 m^3, all oil fuel tanks shall be separated from the outer shell by a distance of not less than 0.76 m. This provision does not apply to small oil fuel tanks with a maximum individual capacity not greater than 30 m^3.
IMO-108.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND aggregate_oil_fuel_capacity_m3 < 600 AND individual_oil_fuel_tank_capacity_m3 > 30, THEN oil_fuel_tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.

IMO-109.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-109.text: For category A and B ships other than oil tankers constructed on or after 1 January 2017, all cargo tanks constructed and utilized to carry oil shall be separated from the outer shell by a distance of not less than 0.76 m.
IMO-109.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ship_type != oil_tanker AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND cargo_tank_carries_oil = true, THEN cargo_tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.

IMO-110.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-110.text: For category A and B oil tankers of less than 5,000 tonnes deadweight constructed on or after 1 January 2017, the entire cargo tank length shall be protected with: double bottom tanks or spaces complying with the applicable requirements of regulation 19.6.1 of MARPOL Annex I; and wing tanks or spaces arranged in accordance with regulation 19.3.1 of MARPOL Annex I and complying with the applicable requirements for distance referred to in regulation 19.6.2 of MARPOL Annex I.
IMO-110.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ship_type = oil_tanker AND deadweight_tonnes < 5000 AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN entire_cargo_tank_length_double_bottom_protection_status = compliant with MARPOL I/19.6.1 AND wing_tank_protection_status = compliant with MARPOL I/19.3.1 and I/19.6.2.

IMO-111.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-111.text: For category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017 all oil residue (sludge) tanks and oily bilge water holding tanks shall be separated from the outer shell by a distance of not less than 0.76 m. This provision does not apply to small tanks with a maximum individual capacity not greater than 30 m^3.
IMO-111.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND tank_type IN {oil_residue_tank, oily_bilge_water_holding_tank} AND individual_tank_capacity_m3 > 30, THEN tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.

IMO-112.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-112.text: In Arctic waters any discharge into the sea of noxious liquid substances (NLS), or mixtures containing such substances, shall be prohibited.
IMO-112.normalized: IF operating_area = Arctic_waters, THEN NLS_or_NLS_mixture_discharge_to_sea = false.

IMO-113.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-113.text: Operation in polar waters shall be taken into account, as appropriate, in the Cargo Record Book, the Manual and the shipboard marine pollution emergency plan for noxious liquid substances or the shipboard marine pollution emergency plan as required by MARPOL Annex II.
IMO-113.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN polar_operation_coverage shall be present in the applicable Cargo Record Book, Manual, and NLS or marine pollution emergency plan.

IMO-114.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-114.text: For category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, the carriage of NLS identified in chapter 17, column e, as ship type 3 or identified as NLS in chapter 18 of the International Code for the Construction and Equipment of Ships Carrying Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk, in cargo tanks of type 3 ships shall be subject to the approval of the Administration. The results shall be reflected on the International Pollution Prevention Certificate for the Carriage of Noxious Liquid Substances in Bulk or Certificate of Fitness identifying the operation in polar waters.
IMO-114.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND carried_NLS_requires_type_3_tank = true AND cargo_tank_type = 3, THEN administration_carriage_approval_status = approved AND applicable_certificate_polar_operation_entry_present = true.

IMO-115.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-115.text: The ship is discharging comminuted and disinfected sewage in accordance with regulation 11.1.1 of MARPOL Annex IV at a distance of more than three nautical miles from any ice-shelf or fast ice and shall be as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10.
IMO-115.normalized: IF sewage_discharge_type = comminuted_and_disinfected, THEN MARPOL_IV_11_1_1_compliance_status = compliant AND distance_to_nearest_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm > 3; record distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1.

IMO-116.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-116.text: The ship is discharging sewage that is not comminuted or disinfected in accordance with regulation 11.1.1 of MARPOL Annex IV and at a distance of more than 12 nautical miles from any ice-shelf or fast ice and shall be as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10.
IMO-116.normalized: IF sewage_discharge_type = not_comminuted_or_disinfected, THEN MARPOL_IV_11_1_1_compliance_status = compliant AND distance_to_nearest_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm > 12; record distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1.

IMO-117.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-117.text: The ship has in operation an approved sewage treatment plant certified by the Administration to meet the operational requirements in either regulation 9.1.1 or 9.2.1 of MARPOL Annex IV, and discharges sewage in accordance with regulation 11.1.2 of Annex IV and shall be as far as practicable from the nearest land, any ice-shelf, fast ice or areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10.
IMO-117.normalized: IF sewage_discharge_uses_treatment_plant = true, THEN sewage_treatment_plant_approval_status = approved, MARPOL_IV_9_1_1_or_9_2_1_certification_status = compliant, MARPOL_IV_11_1_2_discharge_status = compliant, and distances to land, ice shelf, fast ice, and ice concentration greater than 1/10 shall be recorded.

IMO-118.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-118.text: Discharge of sewage into the sea from category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017 and all passenger ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017 is prohibited, except when such discharges are in compliance with paragraph 4.2.1.3 of this chapter.
IMO-118.normalized: IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND (ship_category IN {'A','B'} OR ship_type = passenger_ship), THEN sewage_discharge_to_sea = false UNLESS clause_4_2_1_3_compliance_status = compliant.

IMO-119.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-119.text: Category A and B ships that operate in areas of ice concentrations exceeding 1/10 for extended periods of time, may only discharge sewage using an approved sewage treatment plant certified by the Administration to meet the operational requirements in regulation 9.1.1 or 9.2.1 of MARPOL Annex IV. Such discharges shall be subject to approval by the Administration.
IMO-119.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ice_concentration_tenths > 1 AND extended_period_operation = true AND sewage_discharge_occurs = true, THEN approved_sewage_treatment_plant_used = true, MARPOL_IV_9_1_1_or_9_2_1_certification_status = compliant, and administration_discharge_approval_status = approved.

IMO-120.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-120.text: Discharge into the sea of food wastes is only permitted when the ship is as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10, but in any case not less than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, nearest ice-shelf, or nearest fast ice.
IMO-120.normalized: IF operating_area = Arctic_waters AND food_waste_discharge_to_sea = true, THEN distance_to_nearest_land_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm >= 12 and the distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1 shall be recorded.

IMO-121.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-121.text: Food wastes shall be comminuted or ground and shall be capable of passing through a screen with openings no greater than 25 mm. Food wastes shall not be contaminated by any other garbage type.
IMO-121.normalized: IF food_waste_discharge_to_sea = true, THEN food_waste_comminuted_or_ground = true, required_screen_opening_mm <= 25, and contaminated_by_other_garbage = false.

IMO-122.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-122.text: Food wastes shall not be discharged onto the ice; discharge of animal carcasses is prohibited.

IMO-123.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-123.text: Discharge of cargo residues that cannot be recovered using commonly available methods for unloading shall only be permitted while the ship is en route and where all of the following conditions are satisfied: cargo residues, cleaning agents or additives, contained in hold washing water do not include any substances classified as harmful to the marine environment; both the port of departure and the next port of destination are within Arctic waters and the ship will not transit outside Arctic waters between those ports; no adequate reception facilities are available at those ports; and discharge of cargo hold washing water containing residues shall be made as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10, but in any case not less than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, nearest ice shelf, or nearest fast ice.
