IMO-123.normalized: Cargo-residue discharge is permitted only if residue_not_recoverable_by_common_methods = true, ship_en_route = true, harmful_substance_present = false, departure_and_destination_within_Arctic = true, route_remains_within_Arctic = true, adequate_reception_facilities_available = false, and distance_to_nearest_land_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm >= 12; record distance from ice concentration greater than 1/10.

IMO-124.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-124.text: In the Antarctic area, discharges under regulation 6.1 of MARPOL Annex V shall be as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10, but in any case not less than 12 nautical miles from the nearest fast ice; and food waste shall not be discharged onto ice.
IMO-124.normalized: IF operating_area = Antarctic_area AND MARPOL_V_6_1_discharge = true, THEN distance_to_nearest_fast_ice_nm >= 12 and the distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1 shall be recorded; food_waste_discharge_onto_ice = false.

IMO-125.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
IMO-125.text: Operation in polar waters shall be taken into account, as appropriate, in the Garbage Record Book, Garbage Management Plan and the placards as required by MARPOL Annex V.
IMO-125.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN polar_operation_coverage shall be present in the applicable Garbage Record Book, Garbage Management Plan, and garbage placards.

IMO26-001.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-001.text: This chapter applies to ships certified in accordance with SOLAS chapter I.
IMO26-001.normalized: Polar Code chapter 9 applies only when SOLAS_chapter_I_certified = true.

IMO26-002.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-002.text: This chapter applies to: fishing vessels of 24 metres in length overall and above; pleasure yachts of 300 gross tonnage and upwards not engaged in trade; and cargo ships of 300 gross tonnage and upwards but below 500 gross tonnage.
IMO26-002.normalized: chapter_9_1_applicable = true IF (ship_type = fishing_vessel AND length_overall_m >= 24) OR (ship_type = pleasure_yacht AND gross_tonnage >= 300 AND engaged_in_trade = false) OR (ship_type = cargo_ship AND 300 <= gross_tonnage < 500).

IMO26-003.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-003.text: Ships shall have the ability to receive up-to-date information including ice information for safe navigation.
IMO26-003.normalized: IF chapter_9_1_applicable = true, THEN current_navigation_information_receiving_capability = true AND current_ice_information_receiving_capability = true.

IMO26-004.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-004.text: The navigational equipment and systems shall be designed, constructed and installed to retain their functionality under the expected environmental conditions in the area of operation.
IMO26-004.normalized: IF chapter_9_1_applicable = true, THEN every navigation equipment item shall have environmental_functionality_test_status = passed for the expected operating-area conditions.

IMO26-005.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-005.text: Systems for providing reference headings and position fixing shall be suitable for the intended areas.
IMO26-005.normalized: Every heading-reference and position-fixing system shall have intended_area_suitability_approval_status = approved.

IMO26-006.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-006.text: Ships shall have means of receiving and displaying current information on ice conditions in the area of operation.
IMO26-006.normalized: IF chapter_9_1_applicable = true, THEN ice_information_receiver_present = true, ice_information_display_present = true, and displayed_ice_information_status = current for the operating area.

IMO26-007.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-007.text: Ice-strengthened ships constructed on or after 1 January 2026 shall have either two independent echo-sounding devices or one echo-sounding device with two separate independent transducers. Other devices capable of depth sounding, such as fish finders, acceptable to the Administration, may be used as equivalent means of meeting this requirement.
IMO26-007.normalized: IF ship_ice_strengthened = true AND construction_date >= '2026-01-01', THEN independent_echo_sounding_device_count >= 2 OR (echo_sounding_device_count >= 1 AND independent_transducer_count >= 2) OR administration_approved_equivalent_depth_sounding_device_present = true.

IMO26-008.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-008.text: Ships shall comply with SOLAS regulation V/22.1.9.4, irrespective of the date of construction and the size, and have a clear view astern. On ships which cannot comply with these requirements, arrangements acceptable to the Administration shall be provided to achieve a level of visibility that is equivalent to these requirements.
IMO26-008.normalized: SOLAS_V_22_1_9_4_compliance_status = compliant AND clear_view_astern_status = compliant, OR administration_approved_equivalent_visibility_arrangement_present = true.

IMO26-009.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-009.text: For ships operating in areas, and during periods, where ice accretion is likely to occur, means to prevent the accumulation of ice on antennas required for navigation and communication shall be provided.
IMO26-009.normalized: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN every required navigation or communication antenna shall have ice_accumulation_prevention_means_present = true.

IMO26-010.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-010.text: Where equipment required by SOLAS chapter V or this chapter have sensors that project below the hull, such sensors shall be protected against ice.
IMO26-010.normalized: IF required_sensor_projects_below_hull = true, THEN sensor_ice_protection_present = true.

IMO26-011.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-011.text: In category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2026, the bridge wings shall be enclosed or designed to protect navigational equipment and operating personnel. On ships which cannot comply with this regulation, arrangements acceptable to the Administration shall be provided to achieve a level of protection that is equivalent to this regulation.
IMO26-011.normalized: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2026-01-01', THEN bridge_wings_enclosed = true OR bridge_wing_protection_design_status = approved OR administration_approved_equivalent_bridge_wing_protection_present = true.

IMO26-012.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-012.text: Ships of 500 gross tonnage and upwards shall have two non-magnetic means to determine and display their heading. Both means shall be independent and shall be connected to the ship's main and emergency source of power.
IMO26-012.normalized: IF gross_tonnage >= 500, THEN non_magnetic_heading_means_count >= 2; the means shall be independent and each connected to main_power and emergency_power.
IMO26-012.verification_mode: Conditional qualified count and topology constraint

IMO26-013.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-013.text: Ships proceeding to latitudes over 80 degrees shall be fitted with at least one GNSS compass or equivalent, which shall be connected to the ship's main and emergency source of power.
IMO26-013.normalized: IF planned_or_actual_latitude_deg > 80, THEN GNSS_compass_or_equivalent_count >= 1 AND connected_to_main_power = true AND connected_to_emergency_power = true.

IMO26-014.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-014.text: Ships, with the exception of those solely operating in areas with 24 hours daylight, shall be equipped with two means of illumination to aid visual detection of ice.

IMO26-015.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-015.text: This chapter applies to ships certified in accordance with SOLAS chapter I.
IMO26-015.normalized: Polar Code chapter 11 applies only when SOLAS_chapter_I_certified = true.

IMO26-016.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-016.text: This chapter applies to the following ships operating in polar waters: fishing vessels of 24 metres in length overall and above; pleasure yachts of 300 gross tonnage and upwards not engaged in trade; and cargo ships of 300 gross tonnage and upwards but below 500 gross tonnage.
IMO26-016.normalized: IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN chapter_11_1_applicable = true when (ship_type = fishing_vessel AND length_overall_m >= 24) OR (ship_type = pleasure_yacht AND gross_tonnage >= 300 AND engaged_in_trade = false) OR (ship_type = cargo_ship AND 300 <= gross_tonnage < 500).

IMO26-017.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-017.text: The voyage plan shall take into account the potential hazards of the intended voyage.
IMO26-017.normalized: IF chapter_11_1_applicable = true, THEN voyage_plan_present = true and every intended_voyage_hazard shall have voyage_plan_coverage = true.

IMO26-018.source: Polar Code January 2026 Supplement - Resolution MSC.538(107)
IMO26-018.text: The master shall consider a route through polar waters, taking into account the following: the procedures required by the safety management system on board; if no safety management system is implemented there shall be a documented procedure for operation in polar waters; any limitations of the hydrographic information and aids to navigation available; current information on the extent and type of ice and icebergs in the vicinity of the intended route; statistical information on ice and temperatures from former years; places of refuge; current information and measures to be taken when marine mammals are encountered relating to known areas with densities of marine mammals, including seasonal migration areas; current information on relevant ships' routeing systems, speed recommendations and vessel traffic services relating to known areas with densities of marine mammals, including seasonal migration areas; national and international designated protected areas along the route; and operation in areas remote from search and rescue (SAR) capabilities.
IMO26-018.normalized: IF chapter_11_1_applicable = true, THEN the route planning record shall cover all nine clause 11-1.3 topics; if safety_management_system_implemented = false, documented_polar_operation_procedure_present shall be true.
